meta.method: Four readers walked every hunk of git diff v4.0.0..HEAD by subsystem (classification and domains; structural detection; primers, in-silico PCR, genome scan, fetch and backend; outputs and interface) and checked the code; a catalogue reader mapped the three existing benchmark sets. The outputs/interface records were written from the CHANGELOG and the code. Pending at the time of writing: the measured 4.0.0-vs-4.1.0 behaviour diff over the benchmark caches and the Dfam consensus set, the endpoint-level impact mapping, and two independent checks of this inventory.

frozen_parameters.name: Primer3 Standard preset
frozen_parameters.value: 18-27 nt, Tm 57-63 C, GC 40-60%, product 150-500 bp, 5 candidates

unchanged_behaviours: Bundled profile file te_domains.hmm is byte-identical to v4.0.0 (no diff); panel size 30; scan E-value cut-off 1e-3; MAX_ORFS_SCANNED 12; minimum ORF length 40 aa. Only the code and label of the RVT_3 model changed.

classify._GAG_CORE {Gag_p24, Gag_p24_C, Gag_p10, PEG10_N-capsid}, _CODE_ORDER, _LINE_CORROBORATION {ORF1} and _RETRO_CORROBORATION {RNaseH, ENV, PR} are unchanged (though RNaseH now also receives RVT_3 hits).

Copia and Gypsy canonical domain orders (GAG-PR-INT-RT-RNaseH-ENV and GAG-PR-RT-RNaseH-INT-CHR-ENV) and the rule INT before RT = Copia, INT after RT = Gypsy for a single same-strand non-overlapping integrase are unchanged; High still needs a Copia or Gypsy call with >= 2 domain codes and a resolvable order.

The class (klass) vocabulary (Class I retrotransposon, Class II DNA transposon, unclassified), the confidence vocabulary (High, Moderate, Candidate) and the outcome vocabulary (complete, withheld) are unchanged; no te_class string was added or removed (DNA/unclassified is still emitted by the structure-aware 'DNA transposon' fallback).

The five bundled examples keep their calls: M11240 LTR/Copia High, M12927 LTR/Gypsy High (env-like ORF is TLV_coat-type evidence, still not a withhold), M80343 LINE Moderate (tier 'intact / autonomous-consistent'), X01005 DNA/Tc1-Mariner Moderate (TIR 54, no TSD bare), X05424 DNA/hAT Moderate. Cached public elements AJ289709 (HERV-H, TLV_coat), X01472, M18706, X04456, K01964, U19263, X13291 keep te_class and confidence; AJ289709 (HERV-H) remains LTR/Gypsy High.

HERV-K113 (AY037928) completeness (intact / autonomous-consistent, ERV env-bearing LTR retroelement), is_erv True and the retroviral transcript architecture (leader 968-1141, env 6792-8499, polyprotein intron) are unchanged; retroviral.py has no diff.

MIN_TIR_STANDALONE 20 bp, MIN_TSD/MAX_TSD 2-12, LTR and TIR identity floors 80%, LTR seed window 6000 bp, and the hAT expected TSD length 8 bp are unchanged. CACTA, MULE, IS4-like and generic DDE calls still have no expected TSD length ('not diagnostic').

No Bel-Pao, Retrovirus/ERV or LINE-superfamily (L1, CR1, Jockey) label exists in either version; the classifier still stops at order for those. Helitron remains domain-only: 'Helitron-family helicase present — superfamily not called', te_class unclassified, outcome complete.

The lone-RT refusal (RT without LTR/INT and without GAG/PR/RNaseH/ENV/ORF1 or an EN-RT arrangement) is unchanged: 'reverse transcriptase, class unassigned', Candidate, withheld (but RVT_3 hits now count as RNase H corroboration, see CLS-003).
The 'order' field is retained with its 4.0.0 semantics (None for LINE and unresolved calls); the new fields are additive.
Calls on bare reference elements for tier names: every completeness tier and kind string of 4.0.0 is still emitted except where listed; two tiers and two kinds were added, none removed.
Primer design, in-silico PCR, genome scan, splice and fetch behaviours are outside this scope and not assessed here.

Frozen thresholds with values (v4.0.0 = 4.1.0, AST-identical): MIN_LTR_IDENTITY 80.0; MIN_TIR_IDENTITY 80; MIN_TIR_STANDALONE 20; MIN_TSD 2 and MAX_TSD 12; _LTR_SEED_WINDOW 6000; find_ltr k 13, min_ltr 80, min_anchors 4; _extend x_drop 30 and +1/-2 scoring; find_tir k 11, min_tir 10, max_tir 1000, min_anchors 3; _TIR_SEED_WINDOW value 1200 (was an inline literal, now named); find_polya min_run 8; find_pbs search 44, min_ident 0.55, strong 0.72; find_ppt window 30, min_len 9, min_purine 0.82, max_defects 2; find_polya_signal lo 20, hi 60, min_gt_frac 0.65, min_t 4. The 23 keys sealed in v4.0.0 have identical values in 4.1.0.

Function bodies identical by AST comparison: _termini_motif, _CANONICAL_MOTIF, _NONCANONICAL_MOTIFS, _motif_mismatches, _PRIMER_TRNA (tRNA-Lys3 panel only; no initiator tRNA-Met added), find_ppt, find_polya_signal, _dse_state, _POLYA_HEXAMERS.

LTR and TIR remain mutually exclusive in detect_all: a TIR is searched only when no LTR was accepted. The near-miss row type string 'Sub-threshold terminal direct repeat (advisory)' and its 80.0 threshold are unchanged (only the set of pairs that fall into it changes, STR-001).

Bare specimens give identical structural rows in both versions: M11240.1 LTR 276 bp at 100.0 (span [0,5146]), M12927.1 LTR 482 bp at 100.0 (span [0,7469]), X01005.1 TIR 54 bp at 100.0, X05424.1 TIR 11 bp at 90.9, M80343.1 poly-A tail 27 bp at [6023,6050]; engine superfamily and confidence for these are unchanged. Forward PPT and poly(A)-signal coordinates on the copia and gypsy specimens are unchanged.
Substitution-only LTR pairs are measured as before (300-bp pairs: 20/20 accepted at 5%, 19/20 at 20% in both; accepted counts differ by 1-2 of 60 only between 20% and 22% divergence).

The anchored terminal-path TIR read of bare records is unchanged: synthetic bare TIRs (11/1 mismatch, 13/0, 20/2, 30/3, 15/3 mismatches; 20 seeds each) are found 20/20 with identical lengths and identities in both versions.

Indels longer than 32 bp (deletion or insertion) still halve the LTR to the in-phase part, as in v4.0.0; LTRs of 6 kb or longer remain unseedable; the short/imperfect TIR joint window is 400 bp and a 1200-bp window governs 13-bp exact cores, neither of which widened.
The random-sequence chance-TIR ceiling is unchanged in magnitude (17 bp across 22,500 sequences; 17 bp over 1,800 re-measured), and the 20-bp standalone floor is unchanged.
PBS random-leader rate is unchanged: 23 of 200 random 300-nt leaders return a PBS row in both versions; the reporting floor and confident threshold did not move.

Poly-A tail detection of a clean homopolymer at the record end, and poly-T on the reverse complement, is unchanged (L1.2 27 bp both; A8 and A20 bare tails 20/20 both). A tail followed by a flank with an 8-bp or 6-bp TSD is not called in either version; an uncorroborated tract in a flank (A14 in random flanks) is not a tail in either version.
Lower-case input through the engine gives identical structural rows (the engine already upper-cases); only direct detector callers see the new upper-casing.

TSD search order and range are unchanged (expected length first, then 12 down to 2); a TSD that is a (TA)n flank run is still emitted by detect_all, now with a chance_probability that reads as non-chance.
The domain-panel, ORF and classification logic are not in this scope; the structural rows they consume change as listed, but no classification threshold in structural.py moved.

Primer3 design defaults other than the product range are identical: opt_size 20, min_size 18, max_size 27, opt_tm 60, min_tm 57, max_tm 63, GC 40-60, num_return 5, max_poly_x 4, gc_clamp 0. The four GUI presets are identical (Standard 150-500 bp; qPCR 70-150, Tm 58-62, clamp 1, max size 24; High-specificity 150-500, Tm 60-64, size 20-26, GC 45-60, poly-X 3, clamp 2, 8 pairs; Permissive 100-1000, Tm 52-65, size 18-30, GC 30-70, poly-X 5, 10 pairs).

Untargeted Standard-preset design on a record without ambiguity codes returns the same pairs, products, Tm and penalties (measured on M11240); Primer3's Tm model and condition values are unchanged; primer3-py, pyhmmer, build and backend requirement pins and the backend tool pins (RepeatMasker 4.2.4, Dfam 4.0 file list) show no diff.

oligoqc thresholds (hairpin -2 caution / -9 warn, dimer -5 / -9, 3'-end -6 / -9 kcal/mol), QC conditions (50 mM Na+, 0 Mg2+, 0 dNTP, 250 nM, 37 C), the ViennaRNA cross-check, flag tiers and the hairpin, self-dimer and hetero-dimer values are unchanged (measured hetero-dimer -4.39 Primer3 / -3.14 ViennaRNA in both).

In-silico PCR parameters and rules not listed as changes: max_mm 2, tp 5, min_anneal 18, product window 70-1000, MAX_SITES and MAX_AMPS 4000, intended endpoint tolerance 0, the IUPAC primer-base table, both-strand search, single-primer (F+F, R+R) products and amplicon ranking. For a single sequence with no background, coordinates, mismatches, tails and anneal lengths are identical; anchored_sites without a core argument returns the same sites (tests/test_anchored_equivalence.py).

The specimen's lone-search rule is unchanged: per primer and strand the longest core wins, so a shorter imperfect copy is hidden by a longer perfect site (measured: the background alone as specimen still gives 2 products in both versions).

Genome-scan engine: isPcr min_perfect 15, min_good 15, default product window 4000 (min 0), query row names pair/fwdonly/revonly, isPcr headers 1-based inclusive (confirmed live: the designed span maps onto the real product endpoints), the sealed content (assembly accession, source checksum, isPcr version and parameters) and its independence of any locus; the product set for the same pair and assembly is identical.

Genome-scan primer input still goes through strip().upper() and a DNA/IUPAC regex, not normalize_primer: internal whitespace, U and '-' are rejected in both versions (measured) while lower case is accepted, which is inconsistent with run_pcr after PCR-004.

RepeatMasker invocation (-qq, -pa, -species only when an organism is named, curated library by default, uncurated only when requested) and its hits are identical in both versions (measured on M11240 with a blank organism and with Drosophila melanogaster); Dfam curated-only family counts are unchanged (Homo sapiens 1439, Drosophila melanogaster 399 measured; the rest of the coverage table is not in the diff).

minimap2 splice invocation (-x splice --secondary=no), the canonical splice-site set (GT-AG, GC-AG, AT-AC) and the exon and intron blocks are unchanged; only the strand logic and new fields change (GEN-010).

Fetch: E-utilities endpoints, ENA fallback, coordinate semantics (1-based inclusive efetch seq_start/seq_stop), the 17 curated organisms and 26 bundled assemblies with their pinned accessions, acceptance of ordinary accessions (X04456, M11240.1, NC_003075.7) and the on-disk cache location are unchanged.

Provenance canonicalisation (teagle-json-utf8-v1), manifest schema 0.2 and source-context schema 1.0 are unchanged, and 4.0.0 manifests still verify under 4.1.0 code; every primer, PCR (local-input), annotate and splice manifest hash nevertheless changes (INP-010, INP-011, PRM-001, GEN-006).

The right-click 'Design primers here' on a domain row is unchanged (routed: the domain is Primer3's target and the product flanks and spans it); the Custom range goal over the whole record equals the old untargeted design; the engine API still accepts primer3_target and included_region exactly as in 4.0.0.

benchmarks/score.py remains the frozen 4.0.0 scorer and benchmarks/diff_anchored_sites.py (matcher equivalence harness) is untouched; no 4.1.0 label in this scope (default-lineage species string, on-target tier names, template_ambiguity, annealing_core) is understood by the 4.0.0 scorer.

records.title: Retrovirus-specific capsid/matrix or envelope profiles withhold the Gypsy call (RETROVIRAL_UNDETERMINED)
records.before: In the RT + DDE integrase + accepted paired LTR branch, an integrase C-terminal to the RT on the same strand (non-overlapping) always gave superfamily 'Gypsy (Ty3)' (suffix ' · chromovirus' when a chromodomain was present), te_class LTR/Gypsy, and confidence High when >=2 domain codes and the INT/RT order was resolvable. The identity of the gag or env profile played no role, so HERV-K113 (HML-2) was LTR/Gypsy High and its explanation said 'endogenous retrovirus (ERV) / errantivirus lineage'.
records.after: If the same branch is reached with INT after RT and any detected hit has hmm name in {Gag_p24, Gag_p24_C, Gag_p10, HERV-K_env_2, GP41}, superfamily is the constant RETROVIRAL_UNDETERMINED, te_class LTR/unclassified, confidence Moderate (the Copia/Gypsy High rule needs a Copia or Gypsy superfamily), outcome stays 'complete', is_erv is unchanged (True when an ENV hit and LTRs are present), 'order' keeps the Gypsy-type canonical string (e.g. GAG–PR–RT–RNaseH–INT–ENV), wicker_order is LTR, completeness tier and kind are unchanged ('intact / autonomous-consistent', 'ERV (env-bearing LTR retroelement)' for HERV-K113), and the retroviral transcript architecture (env splice model) is unchanged. An evidence sentence says the Gypsy-type pol order is shared by Gypsy, Bel-Pao and Retrovirus/ERV so the superfamily is not called. Because the superfamily key no longer starts with Copia/Gypsy, no TSD-congruence sentence about LTR target sites is produced. TLV_coat, zf-CCHC_5, PEG10_N-capsid and Chromo do not trigger the withhold. A Copia-order call (INT before RT) is unaffected by a retroviral profile.
records.trigger: Records with an accepted paired LTR row, an RT hit and a same-strand non-overlapping INT hit lying after the RT (translation order), plus at least one hit from the five profile names. In practice HML-2-like betaretroviral gag (Gag_p24/p24_C/p10) or a betaretroviral/lentiviral/gamma-like env hit by HERV-K_env_2 or GP41. Not triggered when INT precedes RT, when no LTR was accepted, when the only gag/env hits are TLV_coat, zf-CCHC_5 or PEG10_N-capsid, or when the INT is on another strand/overlaps the RT.
affected_outputs: classification.superfamily: 'Gypsy (Ty3)' -> RETROVIRAL_UNDETERMINED string for affected inputs
classification.explanation and evidence (new retrovirus-specific sentence; old Gypsy/Ty3 order sentence removed)
classification TSV / RepeatMasker class string / Wicker code and GFF3 TE parent attributes derived from te_class and superfamily
any scorer keyed on the superfamily string (the string is new to the frozen 4.0.0 scorer, which raises on it)
labels_added: LTR retrotransposon (superfamily undetermined; retroviral-type gag/env — Gypsy, Bel-Pao and Retrovirus/ERV are not separated by the bundled panel)
labels_renamed: Gypsy (Ty3) -> RETROVIRAL_UNDETERMINED string (conditional re-label for inputs meeting the trigger; 'Gypsy (Ty3)' is still emitted for other inputs)

parameters.name: _RETROVIRAL_PROFILES (HMM names that withhold Gypsy)
parameters.basis: Wicker et al. 2007 (Gypsy and Retrovirus/ERV are sibling superfamilies sharing the PR-RT-RH-INT pol order); TLV_coat excluded on purpose because it also annotates the env of insect Ty3/gypsy elements (errantiviruses)

parameters.name: _GAG_CORE (capsid/matrix profiles counted as core gag)
parameters.basis: unchanged set; the withhold set is a separate constant

records.measured: Public GenBank record AY037928 (HERV-K113, 9,472 bp; cached fetch), run through engine.analyze in separate processes, both strands: v4.0.0 LTR/Gypsy 'Gypsy (Ty3)' High; 4.1.0 LTR/unclassified, RETROVIRAL_UNDETERMINED, Moderate, outcome complete, is_erv True, order GAG–PR–RT–RNaseH–INT–ENV, completeness 'intact / autonomous-consistent', retroviral architecture identical (leader 968-1141, env 6792-8499, intron 1141-6792). Domains there: Gag_p10, Gag_p24, zf-CCHC_5, RVP, RVT_1, RNase_H, rve, HERV-K_env_2, GP41. Hand-built rows (LTR 0-968/8504-9472; GAG 1141-1390, PR, RT 4130-4613, RNaseH, INT 5804-6095, ENV 6792-8499) and each of the five profile names substituted into an RT+INT+LTR layout give the same switch (8 profile cases: 5 withheld, 3 control profiles keep LTR/Gypsy High). Unchanged between versions: M12927 (mdg4/gypsy) and X01472 (Drosophila gypsy) LTR/Gypsy High, AJ289709 (HERV-H/env62; env hit TLV_coat) LTR/Gypsy High, M11240, M18706 and X04456 LTR/Copia High.
limitations: HERV-H (AJ289709, TLV_coat env) and any retrovirus/ERV whose gag/env is not hit by the five named profiles is still called Gypsy (Ty3) High; the list is five profile names, not a retroviral/non-retroviral discriminator, and the panel has no retroviral RT or integrase profile.
The withheld label sits at confidence Moderate with outcome 'complete' (not Candidate/withheld), so consumers that treat outcome 'withheld' as the abstention signal will not see this as one.
Bel-Pao and Retrovirus/ERV are still never named; the call stops at LTR order.
An insect Ty3/gypsy element that happens to hit Gag_p10 or Gag_p24 would also be withheld (not measured).
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: AY037928 (HERV-K113) and, from the 4.0.0 corpus ERV rows, other HML-2 proviruses such as AY037929 and M14123: 4.0.0 expected LTR/Gypsy High, 4.1.0 expected LTR/unclassified Moderate (verified only for AY037928). Negative/control: M12927 and X01472 (Drosophila gypsy): LTR/Gypsy High in both versions; M11240 and X04456 (Copia) High in both. Boundary: AJ289709 (HERV-H, TLV_coat env) stays LTR/Gypsy High in 4.1.0 (a known residual, expected superfamily Retrovirus/ERV per Wicker). Synthetic: paired 300 bp direct repeats around back-translated RVT_1 consensus then rve consensus (Gypsy order) gives Gypsy High in both versions; adding a back-translated Gag_p24 consensus ORF 5' of the RT is the 4.1.0 trigger (hand-built-row equivalent verified; synthetic with the gag ORF not run).
records.changelog_line: LTR elements whose integrase follows the reverse transcriptase and that carry a retrovirus-specific capsid/matrix or envelope profile hit no longer receive a Gypsy (Ty3) call; the superfamily is reported as not resolved because Gypsy, Bel-Pao and Retrovirus/ERV share that pol order (Wicker et al. 2007), and confidence is capped at Moderate. "Errantivirus" is named only for Gypsy-called elements. Drosophila gypsy keeps its Gypsy call.

records.title: Pfam RVT_3 (PF13456) recoded from reverse transcriptase to an RNase H-like domain
records.before: DOMAIN_INFO['RVT_3'] = ('RT', 'reverse transcriptase', 'retro', 'PF13456'). A hit from the RVT_3 model was reported as domain code RT with label 'reverse transcriptase' and counted as reverse-transcriptase evidence; a back-translated RNase_H or RVT_3 consensus returned an RT hit and a Class I call (retro/unassigned, Moderate).
records.after: DOMAIN_INFO['RVT_3'] = ('RNaseH', 'RNase H-like (Pfam RVT_3)', 'retro', 'PF13456'). The hit is reported as domain code RNaseH with that label (hmm name and pfam accession unchanged) and merges with an overlapping same-strand RNase_H hit under the existing same-code dedup (higher score kept). An RNase H-like region alone no longer licenses a Class I call. The bundled profile file, the 30-model panel size and the E-value are unchanged.
records.trigger: Any ORF in which RVT_3 scores below the E-value cut-off (1e-3), notably RNase H regions and records whose only 'RT' evidence was RVT_3. Records with RVT_1 or RVT_2 hits are unaffected except where an RVT_3 hit was the highest-scoring 'RT' (RT representative used for strand/order tests).

completeness.present/missing lists (RNaseH now includes RVT_3 hits)
domain table exports and GFF3 domain features

domain label 'reverse transcriptase' -> 'RNase H-like (Pfam RVT_3)'

parameters.basis: InterPro/Pfam: PF13456 'Reverse transcriptase-like' sits in the RNase H clan (CL0219) and is integrated under IPR002156 (Ribonuclease H domain); an RNase H-like fold, not the polymerase core

records.measured: Synthetic single-ORF back-translation (recipe R) via engine.analyze. RVT_3 consensus (375 bp): v4.0.0 domains [RNaseH(RNase_H, score 34.3), RT(RVT_3, 183.4)], retro/unassigned, Moderate, tier 'coding evidence present; order unassigned'; 4.1.0 domains [RNaseH(RVT_3, 183.4)], unclassified, Candidate, superfamily 'RNaseH domain(s) detected; no transposable-element assignment', tier 'coding fragment (RNaseH detected; no structural context)'. RNase_H consensus: same switch, domain RNase_H kept in 4.1.0. Hand-built control: RVT_1 + a separate RVT_3 hit: 4.0.0 withheld (lone RT, 'reverse transcriptase, class unassigned', Candidate); 4.1.0 retro/unassigned Moderate complete (see limitations). RVT_1 alone: withheld/Candidate in both.
limitations: Side effect measured on hand-built rows: an RVT_1 RT plus a separate RVT_3 hit was withheld as a lone RT in 4.0.0 but is called 'retrotransposon order unassigned' Moderate in 4.1.0, because RNaseH is in the corroboration set (_RETRO_CORROBORATION); the non-specific RVT_3 hit now corroborates a lone RT.
Elements whose only RT-like hit was RVT_3 lose their Class I call.
No real accession carrying an RVT_3 hit was found among the cached public records, so only synthetic and hand-built cases were run.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: back-translated RVT_3 consensus (recipe R): 4.0.0 retro/unassigned Moderate, 4.1.0 unclassified Candidate. Control: back-translated RVT_1 consensus: unclassified/withheld/Candidate in both. Boundary: an ORF with an RVT_1 region plus an RVT_3 region on the same strand (4.0.0 withheld, 4.1.0 retro/unassigned Moderate).
records.changelog_line: Pfam RVT_3 (PF13456), an RNase H-clan profile, is reported as an RNase H-like domain instead of reverse transcriptase, so an RNase H region alone no longer licenses a Class I call. The panel still has 30 models.

records.title: Overlapping integrase and transposase hits on one strand keep only the stronger
records.before: _dedup_domains kept the best hit per (domain code, strand, overlapping nt region) only. The rve integrase model and DDE transposase models (DDE_3, etc.) cross-score the same DDE fold, so an integrase region also returned a TPase hit; a retroviral integrase consensus gave INT + TPase(DDE_3), a Class II call (DNA/Tc1-Mariner, Moderate), and an LTR element with a cross-scoring TPase hit was flagged composite, capping High at Moderate.
records.after: Where an INT hit and a TPase hit lie on the same strand and overlap by at least half of the shorter span, only the higher-scoring one is kept (symmetric: a stronger TPase also removes a weaker INT). Other code pairs (for example RNaseH with TPase, including the RNase-H-fold hAT models) and opposite strands are untouched.
records.trigger: Records with an rve (INT) region that also scores a TPase profile above the E-value cut-off, or the converse, on the same strand with >=50% overlap of the shorter hit.
affected_outputs: classification class (Class I vs II), te_class, superfamily, confidence, tier, kind for such records
composite flag effect on confidence (High no longer capped when the cross-hit was the only TPase)

parameters.name: INT/TPase shadowing overlap rule
parameters.v4_1_0: same strand and overlap*2 >= shorter span, INT vs TPase only
parameters.basis: INT and TPase are both DDE folds whose models cross-score; the stronger model identifies the region

records.measured: Synthetic (recipe R) rve consensus alone (312 bp): v4.0.0 domains [INT, TPase DDE_3 score 17.7], DNA/Tc1-Mariner Moderate, tier 'partial (transposase present)'; 4.1.0 [INT], retro/partial Candidate, 'coding fragment (INT; RT/transposase not detected)'. Synthetic LTR element (300 bp direct repeats, spacer, rve ORF then RVT_1 ORF, or the reverse): v4.0.0 carried a cross-hit TPase:DDE_3 and returned Gypsy/Copia Moderate; 4.1.0 returns Gypsy/Copia High with no TPase hit. No cached public real element showed an INT/TPase overlap (13 accessions checked), so no real-sequence change was measured.
limitations: A real DDE transposase region where rve outscores the transposase model would now lose its TPase hit and become an INT-only coding fragment (not observed in the cached real elements; untested on a corpus).
The 2x overlap threshold is a heuristic, not a literature value.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: back-translated rve consensus (recipe R): 4.0.0 DNA/Tc1-Mariner Moderate, 4.1.0 retro/partial Candidate. Negative: X01005 (Tc1) and X05424 (Ac): TPase hits intact, calls unchanged. Boundary: a hand-built INT and TPase pair with overlap exactly half the shorter span (kept = stronger one) and a pair on opposite strands (both kept).
records.changelog_line: missing from CHANGELOG

records.title: Withheld or conflicting classifications always report Candidate confidence
records.before: Confidence was forced to Candidate only for conflicting transposase classes. A lone RT beside a TIR, an unattached EN hit or a Helitron helicase (outcome 'withheld') could still show Moderate through the 'rt and (has_ltr or has_tir)' and 'ndom >= 2' rules.
records.after: After the rule ladder, confidence is set to Candidate whenever tpase_conflict, order_conflict, rt_class_withheld or classification_withheld applies. Outcome vocabulary (complete/withheld) and the three confidence values are unchanged. The retroviral-undetermined and nested-integrase conflict labels are NOT in this set: they stay Moderate with outcome complete.
records.trigger: A lone RT with one of: a TIR of any length (including >=20 bp), an EN hit outside an EN-RT arrangement, a Helitron helicase hit; a withheld terminal direct-repeat candidate; the new LINE-vs-LTR order conflict.
affected_outputs: confidence column in tables and exports
records.measured: Hand-built rows: lone RT + 12 bp TIR, + 25 bp TIR, + EN in another ORF, + HEL: v4.0.0 Moderate/withheld, 4.1.0 Candidate/withheld (lone RT alone: Candidate in both). End-to-end synthetic (recipe R): RVT_1 consensus ORF between 25 bp inverted arms: v4.0.0 Moderate, 4.1.0 Candidate, both outcome withheld; same ORF without arms Candidate in both.
limitations: The CHANGELOG states 'withheld outright always reports Candidate', which is true; but the RETROVIRAL_UNDETERMINED and nested-integrase labels are not withheld and report Moderate.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: synthetic RVT_1 consensus ORF with 25 bp terminal inverted repeats (4.0.0 Moderate, 4.1.0 Candidate). Negative: same ORF without arms (Candidate in both). Boundary: arms of 12 bp versus 25 bp (both flip; the TIR length does not matter).
records.changelog_line: A classification that is withheld outright always reports Candidate confidence; terminal repeats no longer raise a transposase-only call to Moderate.

records.title: Terminal direct repeats no longer raise a transposase-only call to Moderate
records.before: The confidence rule '(tpase and (has_ltr or tir_ok))' gave Moderate to a transposase call that had paired terminal DIRECT repeats (LTR row) but no enclosing TIR pair.
records.after: The rule is '(tpase and tir_ok)': only a TIR pair that encloses (or is not contradicted by) the transposase lifts the call from Candidate (when only one domain code) to Moderate. A transposase call with LTR-type direct repeats stays Candidate.
records.trigger: A transposase (TPase) call with an accepted LTR row and no usable TIR; mainly DNA-transposase ORFs inside a segmental/tandem duplication or a mis-scanned flanked window.
affected_outputs: classification.confidence: Moderate -> Candidate for the trigger
records.measured: Hand-built LTR row + one hAT TPase hit: v4.0.0 DNA/hAT Moderate, 4.1.0 Candidate. With a 30 bp TIR instead: Moderate in both.
limitations: Rare input (a transposase together with LTR-type direct repeats and no TIR); no real-sequence case was found in the cached records.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: a hand-built or synthetic hAT transposase ORF flanked by a 300 bp direct-repeat pair (no inverted repeat): 4.0.0 Moderate, 4.1.0 Candidate. Negative: X05424 (Ac, TIR present): Moderate in both. Boundary: 30 bp TIR present together with direct repeats (Moderate in both).
records.changelog_line: A classification that is withheld outright always reports Candidate confidence; terminal repeats no longer raise a transposase-only call to Moderate.

records.title: Nested or adjacent integrases: every same-strand non-overlapping integrase is read against the RT
records.before: Copia versus Gypsy used only the highest-scoring INT hit (_rep) and compared its translation position with the RT's. With several INT hits (nested or adjacent loci) the call followed the best bit score; an INT in another ORF could decide it.
records.after: All INT hits on the RT's strand that do not overlap it are collected. If any lie in the RT's own ORF only those are used. If INT hits remain on both sides of the RT, superfamily is 'LTR retrotransposon (superfamily undetermined)', te_class LTR/unclassified, confidence Moderate and the evidence says the integrase-vs-RT order is conflicting. With one side only, INT before RT gives Copia and INT after RT gives Gypsy as before. A single-INT locus behaves exactly as in 4.0.0. 'order' is None for the conflict case.
records.trigger: Records with an accepted LTR pair, an RT and two or more INT hits on the RT's strand, at least one on each side of the RT, or an extra INT in the RT's own ORF with a stronger INT elsewhere.
affected_outputs: classification.te_class/superfamily (Copia or Gypsy -> LTR/unclassified, or Copia -> Gypsy)
evidence sentence ('integrase hits lie on both sides of the RT ... conflicting')
records.measured: Hand-built rows (RT 3000-3500 orf0 score 90): own-ORF INT 4700-5000 (23) plus upstream INT 1000-1300 orf2 (34): v4.0.0 LTR/Copia High (stronger upstream INT), 4.1.0 LTR/Gypsy. INTs in other ORFs on both sides: 4.0.0 LTR/Copia High, 4.1.0 LTR/unclassified Moderate. Single INT: High Gypsy in both. End-to-end synthetic (recipe R; 300 bp direct repeats around rve consensus, RVT_1 ORF, mutated rve): 4.0.0 Copia Moderate (an additional cross-hit TPase), 4.1.0 LTR/unclassified Moderate with the conflict sentence.
limitations: The own-ORF preference treats an INT in the RT's ORF as decisive even when a second INT lies on the other side.
Only INT hits on the RT's strand count; hits on the other strand are ignored here (a different rule, CLS-008 for YR).
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: synthetic LTR construct (recipe R) with INT-ORF, RT-ORF, INT-ORF in that order on one strand: 4.0.0 Copia/Gypsy by best score, 4.1.0 LTR/unclassified Moderate. Negative: single INT after RT (Gypsy High both) and single INT before RT (Copia High both). Boundary: two INTs on the same side of the RT (call unchanged).

records.title: DIRS-group call requires the RT and tyrosine recombinase on the same strand
records.before: DIRS-group = an RT hit and a YR hit and no INT, with no strand test. The same test gated the DIRS completeness ledger, the structure-free DIRS call and the ERV exclusion (is_erv false when 'yr and not intg').
records.after: yr now means an RT hit and a YR hit that share a strand (_same_strand). Opposite strands give no DIRS call: the lone-RT state applies ('reverse transcriptase, class unassigned', Candidate, outcome withheld) and, in the structure-free path, '{RT–YR} domain(s) detected; transposable-element class unassigned'. The same predicate now gates the DIRS ledger and the ERV exclusion, so an RT(+) with YR(-), an ENV and LTRs can be an ERV (LTR/unclassified) instead of DIRS.
records.trigger: Records with both RT and YR hits on opposite strands (YR on the other strand).
affected_outputs: is_erv (False -> True where ENV and LTRs present)
retroviral stage (now runs for the ERV case)
records.measured: Hand-built rows RT + YR(-): v4.0.0 DIRS Moderate complete, 4.1.0 unclassified Candidate withheld (superfamily 'reverse transcriptase, class unassigned'); same YR on the plus strand: DIRS Moderate in both. Structure-free path: DIRS-group (coding architecture; structure unassessed) -> 'RT–YR domain(s) detected; transposable-element class unassigned'. Case with LTR, RT(+), YR(-), ENV: v4.0.0 DIRS (is_erv False), 4.1.0 LTR/unclassified is_erv True, kind 'ERV (env-bearing LTR retroelement)'. End-to-end synthetic (recipe R; RVT_1 ORF and a reverse-complemented Phage_integrase consensus ORF 1.5 kb apart): 4.0.0 DIRS Moderate, 4.1.0 unclassified Candidate withheld.
limitations: Strand is the only added test; no distance or ORF-proximity criterion, so a same-strand RT and YR kilobases apart is still called DIRS.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: synthetic construct RT ORF (+) and YR ORF (-) (recipe R): 4.0.0 DIRS Moderate, 4.1.0 withheld Candidate. Negative: RT and YR ORFs on the same strand (DIRS Moderate in both). Boundary: LTR + RT(+) + YR(-) + ENV (4.0.0 DIRS, 4.1.0 ERV LTR/unclassified).

records.title: A LINE's tail is credited only on the strand it belongs to; the poly(A)-signal motif row is not a tail
records.before: Any structural row whose type starts with 'poly' counted as a tail (has_polya), regardless of RT strand, and the advisory 'polyA-signal (motif, advisory)' row also started with 'poly'. A plus-strand LINE with a 5' poly-T (or minus-strand LINE with a 3' poly-A) reached 'intact / autonomous-consistent' and Moderate.
records.after: Tail types are matched exactly. A 3' poly-A tail is credited only when the RT hit is on the plus strand, a 5' poly-T only when it is on the minus strand (tail_ok). The opposite tract is reported in the evidence as present but not credited. The tail gates LINE confidence (Moderate if tail_ok else Candidate) and the LINE completeness tier ('intact / autonomous-consistent' needs the credited tail; otherwise 'near-complete (ORF1 + ORF2 endonuclease and RT recovered)'). The advisory polyA-signal motif is never a tail.
records.trigger: A LINE call (te_class LINE) with a poly-A/poly-T row on the strand opposite to the RT, or a polyA-signal row alone.
records.measured: Hand-built (ORF1-EN-RT LINE, 4 strand/tail combinations): matching strand Moderate/'intact' in both; wrong strand v4.0.0 Moderate/'intact', 4.1.0 Candidate/'near-complete'. End-to-end synthetic: M80343 (L1.2, plus strand, 27 bp 3' poly-A) Moderate/'intact' in both; its reverse complement Moderate/'intact' in both; M80343 with the poly-A removed and 30 T prepended: v4.0.0 Moderate/'intact', 4.1.0 Candidate/'near-complete'. polyA-signal motif row alone with ORF1+RT: 4.0.0 Moderate, 4.1.0 Candidate.
limitations: Applies to real inputs only when a tail of the wrong strand is detected, which is uncommon; the common LINE case (tail on the RT strand) is unchanged. Flanked LINE records change for a different reason (CLS-035).
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: synthetic M80343 with the 3' poly-A replaced by a 5' poly-T on the plus strand: 4.0.0 Moderate/intact, 4.1.0 Candidate/near-complete. Negative: M80343 and its reverse complement (unchanged Moderate/intact). Boundary: M80343 without any tail (Candidate in both).

records.title: LINE-specific coding evidence plus paired terminal direct repeats withholds the order (retro/unassigned)
records.before: With an RT, accepted paired LTR-type direct repeats and no integrase, the call was 'LTR retrotransposon (superfamily undetermined)', LTR/unclassified, Moderate, tier 'fragment', kind 'LTR retroelement', even when ORF1p or an accepted EN-RT arrangement was present.
records.after: If ORF1p or an EN-RT arrangement is present with LTRs and no integrase the result is superfamily 'retrotransposon order unassigned', te_class retro/unassigned, Candidate (order_conflict), tier 'coding evidence present; order unassigned', kind 'retroelement (order unassigned)', and the ledger lists ORF1/EN. Evidence names both lines of evidence. wicker_order is 'unassigned'.
records.trigger: Records with accepted LTR rows (including direct repeats from segmental or tandem duplication), an RT, no INT, and ORF1p or an EN-RT pair on one ORF/strand.
labels_renamed: LTR/unclassified + 'LTR retrotransposon (superfamily undetermined)' -> retro/unassigned + 'retrotransposon order unassigned' (for the trigger)
records.measured: Hand-built rows (ORF1+EN+RT, ORF1+RT, EN+RT, each with LTR 0-968/8504-9472): v4.0.0 LTR/unclassified Moderate tier 'fragment'; 4.1.0 retro/unassigned Candidate. End-to-end synthetic (300 bp direct repeats around M80343): v4.0.0 LTR/unclassified Moderate, 4.1.0 retro/unassigned Candidate, tier 'coding evidence present; order unassigned'.
limitations: 'retrotransposon order unassigned' is not in the frozen 4.0.0 scorer vocabulary (it raises).
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: M80343 flanked on both sides by one 300 bp repeat copy (synthetic): 4.0.0 LTR/unclassified Moderate, 4.1.0 retro/unassigned Candidate. Negative: bare M80343 (LINE Moderate, unchanged). Boundary: ORF1-only plus direct repeats (also flips), RT-only plus direct repeats (stays LTR/unclassified, unchanged).

records.title: RT + chromodomain calls use the LTR completeness ledger
records.before: A call placed in the LTR order by RT + chromodomain (no LTR, no integrase; te_class LTR/unclassified) fell into the LINE ledger: kind 'non-LTR retroelement (LINE-like)', tier 'partial (RT only)', with ORF1, EN and the 3' tail listed as missing.
records.after: The LTR ledger gate also accepts te_class starting with LTR (and excludes retro/unassigned); CHR is added to expected/present; tier is 'partial (RT + chromodomain; integrase not confirmed)' and kind 'retroelement (LTR not confirmed)'. The call (LTR/unclassified, confidence) is unchanged.
records.trigger: RT + chromodomain (CHR) with no accepted LTR and no integrase.
labels_renamed: tier 'partial (RT only)' -> 'partial (RT + chromodomain; integrase not confirmed)' (for the trigger)
kind 'non-LTR retroelement (LINE-like)' -> 'retroelement (LTR not confirmed)' (for the trigger)
records.measured: Hand-built RT 100-700 + Chromo 800-950: v4.0.0 LTR/unclassified, tier 'partial (RT only)', kind 'non-LTR retroelement (LINE-like)'; 4.1.0 same call, tier 'partial (RT + chromodomain; integrase not confirmed)', kind 'retroelement (LTR not confirmed)', CHR in present. te_class, confidence and outcome unchanged. (The 4.0.0 benchmark row AF050455 is the corpus case named in the wave record; not re-run.)
limitations: The strand/ORF co-location of CHR with RT is still not required (documented 3.6.0 rule, left for an owner decision).
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: a synthetic ORF with RVT_1 and Chromo consensus segments (recipe R) and no LTR/INT: tier differs between versions. Negative: RT + ORF1 (LINE ledger unchanged). Boundary: RT + CHR with a detected INT (full LTR ledger in both).

records.title: A long terminal inverted repeat beside only host-like domains is again a non-autonomous Class II candidate
records.before: With a TIR of any length and only host-like coding domains (not RT/TPase and none of GAG/ENV/INT/ORF1), the call was 'unclassified', superfamily '{codes} domain(s) detected; no transposable-element assignment', and the TIR was not mentioned. Completeness kind read 'DNA transposon'.
records.after: If the TIR is >= MIN_TIR_STANDALONE (20 bp) the result is Class II, superfamily 'non-autonomous TIR element (superfamily undetermined)', te_class DNA/non-autonomous, Candidate, evidence naming the TIR length, the chance ceiling and the domain (possible captured gene fragment, Pack-MULE). A shorter TIR leaves the call 'unclassified' and adds a sentence that it is too short to attribute. Completeness kind follows the call (see CLS-013).
records.trigger: TIR >= 20 bp and the detected domains are a subset of {CHR, PR, RNaseH, EN (not in EN-RT arrangement), YR}; no RT, TPase, GAG, ENV, INT, ORF1 or HEL. (RNaseH now includes RVT_3 hits, CLS-003.)
labels_renamed: '{codes} domain(s) detected; no transposable-element assignment'/unclassified -> 'non-autonomous TIR element (superfamily undetermined)'/DNA/non-autonomous (for the trigger)

parameters.name: MIN_TIR_STANDALONE (bp, TIR length that licenses a Class II call without transposase)
parameters.basis: above the longest chance inverted repeat measured (17 bp over 22,500 random sequences, 35-65% GC)

records.measured: Hand-built (31 bp TIR + Chromo): v4.0.0 unclassified, 4.1.0 DNA/non-autonomous Candidate. 12 bp TIR + Chromo: unclassified in both, evidence adds 'too short to attribute'. End-to-end synthetic (recipe R): 31 bp inverted arms around a Chromo consensus ORF: v4.0.0 unclassified (kind 'DNA transposon'), 4.1.0 DNA/non-autonomous Candidate; 12 bp arms: unclassified in both, kind 'terminal inverted repeat (class unassigned)' in 4.1.0.
limitations: A long inverted repeat flanking an unrelated host-like domain (for example a gene) is now a Class II candidate; the composition caution (CLS-021) is the only brake.
The 4.0.0 label 'DNA/non-autonomous' with a plain long TIR and no domain at all is unchanged.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: synthetic 31 bp inverted arms around a back-translated Chromo consensus (recipe R): 4.0.0 unclassified, 4.1.0 DNA/non-autonomous. Negative: 12 bp arms (unclassified both). Boundary: 19 bp versus 20 bp arms (the 20 bp floor is unchanged).

records.title: Completeness kind follows the call (no 'DNA transposon' for a solo LTR or a short TIR)
records.before: For records with an LTR or TIR row but no RT/transposase, completeness.kind was 'LTR retroelement' if an LTR row existed, else 'DNA transposon' regardless of the call. A solo copia LTR (276 bp, TIR scan trips), a short TIR beside GAG or EN, or a Helitron with a TIR all read 'DNA transposon'.
records.after: kind is 'LTR retroelement' if an LTR row exists; 'DNA transposon' if te_class starts with DNA/; 'retroelement fragment (order unassigned)' if te_class starts with retro; otherwise 'terminal inverted repeat (class unassigned)'. Tier strings are unchanged.
records.trigger: Records with a TIR row (no LTR row) whose te_class is not DNA/*: solo LTRs, TIRs shorter than 20 bp, TIR + non-transposase domains, Helitron + TIR.
labels_renamed: kind 'DNA transposon' -> 'terminal inverted repeat (class unassigned)' or 'retroelement fragment (order unassigned)' (for the trigger)
records.measured: M11240[:276] (solo copia 5' LTR) end-to-end: v4.0.0 te_class repeat/structural-only, kind 'DNA transposon'; 4.1.0 same class, kind 'terminal inverted repeat (class unassigned)'. Hand-built: 25 bp TIR + GAG: kind 'DNA transposon' -> 'retroelement fragment (order unassigned)'; 12 bp TIR + EN or + Chromo or YR: -> 'terminal inverted repeat (class unassigned)'; 12 bp TIR alone with no domain: -> 'terminal inverted repeat (class unassigned)'.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: M11240[:276] (public GenBank copia 5' LTR): kind changes. Negative: X01005 (kind 'DNA transposon' in both). Boundary: TIR of 19 vs 20 bp with no domain (kind 'terminal inverted repeat (class unassigned)' vs 'DNA transposon' in 4.1.0).

records.title: Failed protein-domain scan withholds every structure-only call
records.before: With domains_ok False and no RT/TPase evidence, a TIR record was called 'non-autonomous TIR element' / DNA/non-autonomous (outcome complete, 'no coding domain detected' in the ledger), a poly-A-only or empty record 'no clear TE signature' (te_class none), asserting an absence from a scan that never ran. A no-signal record with credited rows was 'complete'.
records.after: With domains_ok False: a TIR record gives superfamily 'terminal inverted repeat, class unassigned', te_class repeat/structural-only, outcome withheld, Candidate, completeness tier 'structural-only (protein-domain scan unavailable; coding content unassessed)' with 'protein domains' unassessed; any other structure-only or empty record gives 'classification withheld (protein-domain scan unavailable)', te_class unclassified, outcome withheld, completeness null. The explanation starts 'Classification withheld'. domains_ok True behaviour is unchanged.
records.trigger: domains_ok False (the domain stage failed, e.g. pyhmmer missing or erroring) and no RT/INT/TPase evidence.
labels_renamed: 'no clear TE signature' -> 'classification withheld (protein-domain scan unavailable)' (domains_ok False)
'non-autonomous TIR element (superfamily undetermined)' -> 'terminal inverted repeat, class unassigned' (domains_ok False)
records.measured: Hand-built domains_ok False: 31 bp TIR: v4.0.0 DNA/non-autonomous complete, 4.1.0 repeat/structural-only withheld; poly-A only and empty rows: 'no clear TE signature' (te_class none) -> 'classification withheld (protein-domain scan unavailable)' (unclassified, withheld). End-to-end with pyhmmer forced unavailable (domains.pyhmmer=None): X01005 v4.0.0 DNA/non-autonomous complete, 4.1.0 terminal inverted repeat class unassigned, withheld, processing.classification 'withheld', retroviral 'not_run'; M11240 stays 'terminal direct-repeat candidate' withheld in both.
limitations: Only the failed-stage case is handled; a domain stage that 'ran' on zero ORFs (status not_run, CLS-029) is still classified as if searched.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: any record analysed with the domain scan disabled (fault injection, not an input property): X01005 gives DNA/non-autonomous (4.0.0) vs withheld TIR candidate (4.1.0). Negative: the same record with the scan working (Tc1/Mariner both). Boundary: LTR-only record (withheld candidate in both).

records.title: Missing pyhmmer is reported as a failed domain stage, not as 'no domains detected'
records.before: scan_domains returned [] when pyhmmer could not be imported; the engine recorded domains status 'complete' (count 0, orfsScanned = ORF count) and the call read as a complete negative.
records.after: scan_domains raises RuntimeError('pyhmmer unavailable: ...'); the engine records processing.domains {'status':'failed','errorType':'RuntimeError'}, adds the note 'domain scan unavailable: RuntimeError', passes domains_ok False to classify (CLS-014) and the top-level status becomes complete_with_stage_failures.
records.trigger: Environments where pyhmmer is absent or broken (frozen build with a packaging fault, hermetic CI without the package).
records.measured: engine.analyze with domains.pyhmmer set to None on M11240: v4.0.0 status complete, domains complete (11 ORFs scanned, 0 hits); 4.1.0 status complete_with_stage_failures, domains failed, note present, domains_unavailable True. Same on X01005 (see CLS-014).
limitations: Fault-injection only; not an input property, so a benchmark on bundled data cannot trigger it.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: run any element with pyhmmer made unimportable. Negative: normal environment (identical). Boundary: a record with zero ORFs (domain status not_run, not failed; CLS-029).

records.title: Structure-free transposase call carries the advisory strongest-profile family
records.before: When structural detection failed (structural_ok False) a transposase hit always gave superfamily 'DNA transposon (transposase detected; termini unassessed)' and te_class DNA/unclassified; the family of the strongest hit was ignored and conflicts were not noted.
records.after: The strongest-hit family mapping is a shared helper (_tpase_family). The structure-free call is '{family} (advisory: strongest transposase profile; termini unassessed)' with te_class DNA/{hAT|Tc1-Mariner|CACTA|MULE|IS4-like|DDE|unclassified}, Candidate, termini listed as unassessed, and a ledger sentence when several transposase classes are detected. The structure-aware path uses the same helper with unchanged output. wicker_order is TIR.
records.trigger: structural_ok False (structural stage failed) with a TPase hit and no RT.
labels_added: {family} (advisory: strongest transposase profile; termini unassessed) with family in: hAT, Tc1/Mariner, CACTA (En/Spm), MULE (Mutator), IS4-like DDE (piggyBac group), DDE transposon, DNA transposon
labels_renamed: 'DNA transposon (transposase detected; termini unassessed)' -> '{family} (advisory: strongest transposase profile; termini unassessed)'
te_class DNA/unclassified -> DNA/{family token} on the structure-free path
records.measured: Hand-built structural_ok False with one hAT TPase: v4.0.0 DNA/unclassified 'DNA transposon (transposase detected; termini unassessed)'; 4.1.0 DNA/hAT 'hAT (advisory: ...)'. CACTA: DNA/CACTA 'CACTA (En/Spm) (advisory: ...)'. Two classes (hAT strongest + Tc1/Mariner): DNA/hAT with the ambiguity sentence.
limitations: Fault-injection path only (structural stage failure); the frozen 4.0.0 scorer raises on all seven advisory labels.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: any hAT record with the structural stage disabled. Negative: same record with structure working (DNA/hAT 'hAT', Moderate with TIR). Boundary: two transposase classes of different score.

records.title: TSD congruence uses superfamily length ranges and a required motif (Tc1/Mariner TA)
records.before: TSD_EXPECT held a single exact expected length per superfamily (Copia 5, Gypsy 5, hAT 8, Tc1/Mariner 2); tsd_congruence(length, superfamily) judged congruent only when length == expected and took no motif. A 4 or 6 bp TSD on a Copia/Gypsy call was 'incongruent'; any 2 bp repeat on Tc1/Mariner was congruent; the LTR incongruence sentence said 'likely coincidental' and quoted 'duplicate 5 bp'.
records.after: TSD_EXPECT entries are (preferred length, accepted range, basis, required motif): Copia and Gypsy 5 (4-6), hAT 8 (8-8), Tc1/Mariner 2 (2-2) with motif TA. tsd_congruence(length, superfamily, motif=None) is congruent when length is in range and (if a motif is supplied and one is required) the motif matches; otherwise incongruent. classify passes the TSD row's motif; the sentences quote the accepted range and motif ('duplicate 4-6 bp', '2 bp (GC) where Tc1/Mariner elements duplicate 2 bp (TA)') and say the repeat may be coincidental or the boundary/superfamily call may be wrong. The preferred length is still what _refine_tsd asks find_tsd for. Superfamilies absent from the table (CACTA, MULE, IS4-like, DDE, unclassified) remain 'not diagnostic'.
records.trigger: Any LTR (Copia/Gypsy) or DNA (hAT, Tc1/Mariner) call with a TSD row.
affected_outputs: TSD row tsd_congruence verdict (congruent/incongruent) for 4 and 6 bp LTR TSDs and for non-TA 2 bp Tc1/Mariner TSDs
labels_renamed: evidence 'likely coincidental' -> 'the repeat may be coincidental, or the boundary or superfamily call may be wrong'

parameters.name: TSD_EXPECT['Copia']
parameters.basis: Wicker et al. 2007 Nat Rev Genet 8:973-982 (4-6 bp for LTR retrotransposons), checked against the HML-2 survey; 5 bp preferred per Ou et al. 2019 Genome Biol 20:275

parameters.name: TSD_EXPECT['Gypsy']
parameters.basis: same as Copia

parameters.name: TSD_EXPECT['hAT']
parameters.basis: Ou et al. 2019

parameters.name: TSD_EXPECT['Tc1/Mariner']
parameters.basis: Wicker et al. 2007 (TA target site defines the superfamily)

parameters.name: MIN_TSD / MAX_TSD
parameters.basis: search range unchanged

records.measured: Hand-built rows: Copia with a 4 bp or 6 bp TSD: v4.0.0 incongruent ('duplicate 5 bp'), 4.1.0 congruent; 2 bp TSD on Copia: incongruent in both, now quoting '4-6 bp'; Tc1/Mariner with 2 bp TA: congruent in both; with 2 bp GC: congruent in 4.0.0, incongruent in 4.1.0 (text names 'GC' versus 'TA'). End-to-end, 30 flanked records per cell (300 bp random flanks, X01005/M11240/M12927 with planted TSDs): Copia 5 bp TSD congruent 15/30 (4.0.0) vs 29/30 (4.1.0); Copia 6 bp 9/30 vs 29/30; Gypsy 5 bp 20/30 vs 30/30; Copia 4 bp 0/30 vs 29/30. These end-to-end shifts also reflect LTR boundary snapping (CLS-035/structural scope), not only the range.
limitations: The 4-6 bp LTR range is citation-based, not fitted to a corpus.
A 5 bp TSD on an LTR element is flagged chance_level True in 4.1.0 (search-adjusted probability), though the LTR congruent sentence does not use that flag.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: flanked M11240 with a planted 4 bp or 6 bp TSD (synthetic flanks around the public GenBank copia record): 4.0.0 incongruent, 4.1.0 congruent. Negative: planted 5 bp (congruent both once the boundary is placed). Boundary: planted 3 bp (incongruent both), and a Tc1/Mariner call with a GC 2 bp TSD (4.0.0 congruent, 4.1.0 incongruent).
records.changelog_line: TSD congruence uses superfamily length ranges (LTR 4–6 bp, preferred 5 bp) and motifs (Tc1/Mariner TA), and a short chance-level repeat is no longer described as proof that the insertion site is captured.

records.title: Tc1/Mariner TIR trimmed to the true arms and TA target site recovered inside classify
records.before: On a flanked Tc1/Mariner record the TIR arms run 2 bp through the palindromic TA target site (tir_len 56-58 instead of 54) and either no TSD row exists or a chance 3 bp repeat (for example GTA) is flagged incongruent. Nothing in classify trimmed the arms.
records.after: After an unambiguous Tc1/Mariner call (not when transposase classes conflict) and a credited TIR row with the record sequence, classify calls structural.palindromic_target_site with the TA motif and updates the TIR row in place (arms trimmed up to 6 bp until TA flanks both ends, boundary_adjustment recorded) and sets or inserts a single TSD row (length 2, motif TA, tsd_congruence congruent). The TSD row carries selected_for_motif True when the arms were trimmed to expose the motif, chance_level True (2 bp), and the evidence says the TA match is by construction and not independent evidence. has_tsd, tir_encloses_tpase and tir_ok are recomputed. Gated on the call: hAT or other superfamilies are never trimmed. Bare records (no flanks) return no TSD and are unchanged.
records.trigger: Flanked records (genomic windows) that classify as Tc1/Mariner with a detected TIR and a TA at the trimmed element boundaries.
affected_outputs: structural TIR row: tir_len (56-58 -> 54), five_prime/three_prime/element_span, boundary_adjustment, identity
TSD row: added or replaced (length 2, motif TA, tsd_congruence congruent, selected_for_motif, chance_level True)
GFF3 TE feature span and TSD rows

parameters.name: _TIR_TRIM_MAX / palindromic_target_site max_trim (bp)
parameters.basis: arms found by extension may run through the target site by at most a few bp

records.measured: engine.analyze on X01005 (Tc1, GenBank) with 300 bp random flanks and a planted TA TSD, 30 seeds: v4.0.0 TIR 54 bp in 0/30 (TIR 56-57, TA TSD row 0/30, one 3 bp GTA row), 4.1.0 TIR exactly 54 bp 30/30 and a 2 bp TA TSD row 30/30 (all congruent, chance_level True, selected_for_motif True, evidence hedged). Controls (30 each): no TSD, random flanks: no TA TSD fabricated in 30/30 (TIR 54 in 24/30 in both versions); planted GC TSD: no trim in either version (TIR 54 0/30 both); planted random 3 bp TSD: TIR 54 in 25/30 both, incongruent 25/30 both. Bare X01005: TIR 54, no TSD, unchanged.
limitations: A 2 bp TA is always chance level (p about 0.06-0.29), so the recovered TSD is congruent by construction and is not credited as insertion-site evidence; completeness tier is unchanged.
The trim is skipped when transposase classes conflict, and applies only to a Tc1/Mariner call; flanked mariner-like elements called another superfamily keep arms 2 bp too long.
The recovered TA TSD is reported as congruent although the search required TA; selected_for_motif is the only flag.
Inserting the TSD row after classification desynchronises processing.structural.count (CLS-032).
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: public GenBank X01005 with 300 bp random flanks and TA TSD (synthetic flanks): 4.0.0 TIR 56-57 no TA TSD, 4.1.0 TIR 54 and 2 bp TA TSD. Negative: the same element with no TSD between random flanks (no TSD fabricated; 24/30 TIR 54 in both), and flanked X05424 (hAT; never trimmed). Boundary: GC 2 bp TSD (unchanged, no trim) and a 3 bp random TSD (incongruent both).
records.changelog_line: Terminal inverted repeats are located in records that carry genomic flanks, and a Tc1/Mariner element reports its true TIR and the TA target site; poly-A tails followed by flank or interrupted by one base are found, with chance tails controlled for multiple testing.

records.title: Refined TSD keeps the boundary-placement count of the span it flanks
records.before: _refine_tsd re-ran find_tsd(seq, up[1], dn[0], expect=exp) and tsd.update(refined) in place; TSD rows had no chance_probability, n_tests or chance_level at all.
records.after: find_tsd takes placements and the refined row inherits the LTR or TIR row's boundary_tests (36 for a snapped LTR), so the refined TSD's chance_probability, n_tests (lengths x placements) and chance_level reflect the multiple testing of the boundary. The re-detection preference for the superfamily's target-site length (shorten a coincidental longer TSD, never lengthen) is unchanged.
records.trigger: Flanked LTR or TIR records with a TSD row and a Copia, Gypsy, hAT or Tc1/Mariner call.
affected_outputs: TSD row chance_probability, n_tests, chance_level (new fields; value after refinement)
records.measured: End-to-end flanked records (30 per cell): Copia with a 5 bp planted TSD carries chance_level True in 29/30 (4.0.0: key absent); Gypsy 5 bp True 30/30; hAT 8 bp False 28/30; LINE 12 bp False 30/30. Copia 6 bp: False 17/30, True 12/30.
limitations: A correctly detected 5 bp LTR TSD is flagged chance-level (search-adjusted), which a UI badge could read as weak evidence; the LTR evidence text does not use the flag.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: flanked M11240 with a 5 bp TSD: TSD row has chance_level True in 4.1.0 and no chance fields in 4.0.0. Negative: flanked M80343 with a 12 bp TSD (chance_level False). Boundary: 6 bp versus 5 bp TSD (a 6 bp TSD is often below the chance-level threshold).
records.changelog_line: Target-site duplication rows carry a chance probability adjusted for every length and boundary placement searched, and structural rows carry their TSD state (found, absent, partially assessable, not assessable, not assessed).

records.title: Empty and all-N records are invalid with a stated reason and are not classified

records.after: A record with no A/C/G/T is invalid with invalidReason ('empty record (a header with no sequence)' or 'no informative bases (only N and ambiguity codes)'), all stages not_run, classification null; with no other valid record the run status is no_valid_records and the warning names the skipped record. The result schema is 1.1; 1.0 documents (no invalidReason, no domains not_run) still validate under 4.0.0 rules.

records.measured: engine.analyze on '>a' and '>a' + 300 N: v4.0.0 status complete, valid True, 'no clear TE signature'; 4.1.0 status no_valid_records, valid False with the reasons above.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: '>a\n' and 300 N. Negative: any normal record (unchanged). Boundary: 300 N plus a single A (valid, classified).

records.title: LTR cis-element orientation taken from the RT/INT/TPase strand when the structure cannot orient the element
records.before: structural.detect_all ran once without an orientation; an LTR row with cis_orientation 'undetermined' kept no PBS/PPT/poly(A)-signal rows on the right strand.
records.after: After the domain scan, if every RT, INT and TPase hit shares one strand and the LTR row's cis_orientation is 'undetermined', detect_all is re-run with orientation=that strand; the new LTR row carries cis_orientation_source 'domain-strand'; a cis-element-determined orientation is never overridden; a failure keeps the first result and adds a note. Shared with the structural/cis-element scope.
records.trigger: Records with an accepted LTR whose cis-elements do not fix the orientation and whose RT/INT/TPase hits are unanimous in strand (typically a reverse-complemented element).
affected_outputs: structural rows PBS, PPT, polyA-signal and their strand
records.measured: Reverse complements of cached public records, engine.analyze: AY037928_rc gains PBS and PPT rows (LTR 968 bp unchanged); AJ289709_rc gains PBS and PPT; X04456_rc (copia) gains PPT; X01472_rc: polyA-signal row replaced by PPT. Forward-strand records: structural rows unchanged for these accessions. Classification calls unchanged in all of them.
limitations: Mixed-strand domain hits give no vote; a nested element on the other strand blocks the re-orientation.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: reverse complement of X04456 (PPT appears in 4.1.0 only). Negative: forward X04456 (unchanged) and a record whose PBS fixes the orientation. Boundary: RT and INT hits on opposite strands (no vote).
records.changelog_line: LTR cis-elements (PBS, PPT, poly(A) signal) are reported on the element's own strand, using the domain strand when the structure alone cannot orient the element.

records.title: Knock-on: flanked-record structural changes alter classification confidence, tier, TSD verdicts and evidence
records.before: On records carrying genomic flanks, detect_all missed the TIR of flanked hAT/Ac elements (TSD 0/30), mislocated the TSD of LTR elements, and found no poly-A tail or TSD for a flanked LINE (confidence Candidate, tier 'near-complete (ORF1 + ORF2 endonuclease and RT recovered)').
records.after: Structural scope changes (flank-aware TIR search, boundary snapping with the TSD, poly-A tail with chance-controlled flank TSD) feed the unchanged classify rules: a flanked LINE with a credited 3′ tail reaches Moderate and 'intact / autonomous-consistent'; flanked hAT records get a TSD row and the 'captured' sentence; flanked LTR records get congruent 4-6 bp TSDs; a 49.7 kb human window changes from 'no clear TE signature' to a withheld 'terminal direct-repeat candidate (LTR origin unconfirmed)' because a sub-threshold pair became an accepted LTR row.
records.trigger: Records with flanking genomic sequence (coordinate fetches, genome windows); bare reference elements are unchanged. Detailed detector changes belong to the structural-scope records.
affected_outputs: classification.confidence and completeness.tier for flanked LINEs
TSD congruence/evidence for flanked LTR and hAT
te_class/outcome for windows where an LTR row appears or disappears
labels_renamed: 'no clear TE signature' (none, complete) -> 'terminal direct-repeat candidate (LTR origin unconfirmed)' (repeat/structural-only, withheld) for one cached 49.7 kb human coordinate window
records.measured: engine.analyze, 30 seeded flanked records per cell (300 bp random flanks around bundled public records): M80343 with a 12 bp TSD: v4.0.0 Candidate in 30/30 (no tail/TSD), 4.1.0 Moderate in 30/30 (tail 27 bp and 12 bp TSD found, tier 'intact / autonomous-consistent'); M80343 with no TSD: Candidate in both (30/30). X05424 with 8 bp TSD: DNA/hAT Moderate in both, TSD row 0/30 -> 28/30. M11240/M12927 calls unchanged (LTR/Copia, LTR/Gypsy High, 30/30 each). Cached public coordinate windows: five of seven unchanged, one (human, 49,721 bp) changed class as above, one yeast 12,001 bp window kept LTR/Copia High with LTR 325 -> 334 bp and a 5 bp TSD found.

records.benchmark_probe: Positive: flanked M80343 (300 bp random flanks, 12 bp TSD): Candidate (4.0.0) vs Moderate/intact (4.1.0). Negative: bare M80343 (Moderate/intact both) and flanked M80343 without TSD (Candidate both). Boundary: flanked X05424 with a 7-10 bp TSD.
records.changelog_line: Terminal inverted repeats are located in records that carry genomic flanks, and a Tc1/Mariner element reports its true TIR and the TA target site; poly-A tails followed by flank or interrupted by one base are found, with chance tails controlled for multiple testing.

records.title: Whole-genome scan: the on-target product is the one at the designed product's genome position
records.before: The engine took design_locus entries {accession, start, stop} as a window and marked as the single on-target the pair product with the largest overlap with any window (ties to the lowest start); any product overlapping the window could win, including a long product spanning the designed one. The shipped panel built the locus from state['source'].regions, whose normalised entries carry 'end', not 'stop', and read 'stop', so the engine received stop = None (coerced to 0) and a window [0, start]: the true product at positions above start overlapped nothing and was called off-target (tier intended-locus-negative). The panel also sent every fetched region.
records.after: A locus entry is {accession, start, end, strand (1/2 or +/-), intended_product_span [a, b), intended_endpoint_tolerance_bp}: the fetched window (1-based inclusive) plus the designed product's 0-based half-open span inside the fetched record. _design_loci maps it to genome coordinates, strand-aware: forward lo = start + a, hi = start + b - 1; reverse lo = end - b + 1, hi = end - a. Exactly one product is marked on_target: the non-single-primer product on the same sequence whose two endpoints are within the tolerance (default 0 bp), smallest error then lowest start; a designed product that is absent promotes nothing (tier intended-locus-negative). An entry lacking accession, window ends, strand or span names no intended product and is ignored (has_locus False, neutral priming sites); a bad strand or an inconsistent span is a BadRequest. The panel sends the locus only for a pair whose own sealed design input is a one-region coordinate fetch of the assembly being scanned and whose record is still on screen (the region the pair was designed on in a multi-region fetch). Labelling is derived and outside the seal.
records.trigger: Whole-genome scan of a pair designed on a specimen fetched by coordinate from the scanned assembly; any engine caller that sends design_locus.
labels_removed: design_locus.stop as the window end (a legacy 'stop' is still read for 'end' but a locus without span/strand is now ignored)

parameters.name: on-target rule
parameters.v4_0_0: largest overlap with the fetched window
parameters.v4_1_0: both endpoints within tolerance of the mapped designed product
parameters.basis: the designed product is the intended target

parameters.name: intended_endpoint_tolerance_bp
parameters.basis: design geometry tolerance

parameters.name: isPcr min_perfect / min_good
parameters.basis: isPcr defaults, unchanged

records.measured: Live (this audit; WSL backend with yeast R64, GCF_000146045.2, prepared; NCBI coordinate fetch): window NC_001136.10:100001-102000 fetched on the + and the - strand, first Standard-preset pair (150-500 bp); real isPcr returns exactly one product, NC_001136.10 100394-100812 (419 bp, 1-based inclusive), on both strands. 4.1.0: on_target True, tier intended-only ('1 on-target product; no additional priming site detected in this assembly under current settings'). 4.0.0 as the shipped panel sent the locus (emulated by posting {accession, start, stop: None}; not a GUI run): on_target False, tier intended-locus-negative ('1 off-target candidate priming site(s); no product at the intended locus under current settings'). Mocked isPcr output, engine called directly, window NC_1:1000-3000, designed span [500,700): products 1500-1699 (designed), 1101-1900 (spanning), NC_9:1500-1699. 4.0.0 with a well-formed {start 1000, stop 3000}: the spanning 1101-1900 product is on-target; 4.1.0: 1500-1699. Reverse-strand fetch (span maps to 2301-2500): 4.0.0 marks 1500-1699, 4.1.0 marks 2301-2500. Designed product absent but spanning product present: 4.0.0 intended-only, 4.1.0 intended-locus-negative. Off-by-one product 1501-1700: 4.0.0 on-target; 4.1.0 off-target at tolerance 0, on-target at tolerance 1. Window-only locus (no span/strand): 4.0.0 marks the spanning product, 4.1.0 neutral (has_locus False, tier limited-site). Two equal copies, designed second: 4.0.0 marks the left copy, 4.1.0 the second. The sealed manifest is identical with and without a locus in both versions.
limitations: On-target needs exact endpoint agreement (tolerance 0 by default); a product shifted one base is off-target.
If fetched sequence names (RefSeq NC_) differ from the scanned assembly's names (e.g. GenBank GCA names) nothing can be on-target; the panel then says the split is not assessed.
Only single-region coordinate-fetched designs carry a locus; single-primer products are never on-target.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: fetch S. cerevisiae chrIV:100,001-102,000 (assembly GCF_000146045.2, + or - strand), design with the Standard preset, take the first pair, scan against the prepared genome with the locus built from the fetch: 4.1.0 labels the single 419-bp product NC_001136.10:100394-100812 on-target; a 4.0.0-style request labels it off-target. Negative: same pair, specimen pasted without a fetch (no locus): both versions neutral (limited/single-site tiers, n_on_target 0). Boundary: shift the designed span by one base with tolerance 0 (off-target) and 1 (on-target); and a designed span that matches a second equal-length copy.
records.changelog_line: The whole-genome scan labels as on-target the product at the designed product's genome position, mapped strand-aware through the fetched window; this was verified against real isPcr output.

records.title: Genome-scan verdicts state single-primer products and name an intended-locus miss
records.before: With no forward+reverse product the verdict said there was no genome-wide product and that the primers do not amplify anywhere in the assembly, even when F+F or R+R products existed; with one on-target product it said no additional priming site was detected regardless of single-primer products.
records.after: n_single is counted and, when above zero, '; N single-primer (F+F/R+R) product(s) also predicted' is appended to every verdict; the sentences 'no additional priming site', 'do not amplify anywhere' and 'no genome-wide priming site' are not emitted while a single-primer product exists. The has_locus zero-product verdict becomes 'no forward+reverse product at the intended locus or elsewhere in this assembly under current settings'. Tier names and thresholds (none, single-site, limited-site (2-5), many-site (>5), intended-only, limited-off-target, many-off-target, intended-locus-negative) are unchanged and still pair-based.
records.trigger: Scans whose product set contains single-primer rows or no pair product.
labels_renamed: 'no genome-wide product - the primers do not amplify anywhere in this assembly' -> 'no forward+reverse product at the intended locus or elsewhere in this assembly under current settings'
'1 on-target product; no additional priming site detected ...' -> '... no additional forward+reverse product detected ... ; N single-primer ... predicted' (when single-primer products exist)
'no genome-wide priming site (...)' -> 'no forward+reverse priming-site pair in this assembly, at the current 3' match length; N single-primer ...' (when single-primer products exist)

parameters.name: tier thresholds (limited vs many sites/off-targets)
parameters.basis: unchanged

records.measured: Run in this audit (genomepcr.summarize on synthetic amplicon rows): single-primer product only, has_locus True: 4.0.0 'no genome-wide product - the primers do not amplify anywhere in this assembly', 4.1.0 'no forward+reverse product at the intended locus or elsewhere in this assembly under current settings; 1 single-primer (F+F/R+R) product(s) also predicted' (tier none in both). One on-target plus one single-primer product: 4.0.0 '1 on-target product; no additional priming site detected in this assembly under current settings', 4.1.0 '... no additional forward+reverse product detected ...; 1 single-primer (F+F/R+R) product(s) also predicted' (tier intended-only in both). No products, no locus: identical in both.
limitations: The tier still ignores single-primer products, so intended-only can coexist with predicted single-primer products.

A named organism keeps its name and gains lineage_searched / lineage_taxid. The advice for an unknown name now says 'leave the organism blank to use RepeatMasker's default lineage (Homo sapiens)'. The RepeatMasker command and its hits are unchanged.

every annotate and genome_annotate manifest hash for blank-organism runs

records.title: Backend failure handling: a dead WSL session fails annotation; probe timeouts give plain errors; 'backend not ready' names the failing condition
records.before: annotate parsed whatever came back: a session that died (return code 4294967295, empty output) or returned exit 1 beside an 'EXIT 0' marker produced ok True with 0 hits, which could be sealed; the not-ready error read 'not ready (RepeatMasker=None, Dfam=False)'.
records.after: annotate requires the EXIT marker and a zero session return code (the script ends with exit $ec) and otherwise returns ok False ('the WSL session ended before RepeatMasker reported, so nothing was searched' or 'RepeatMasker reported success but the WSL session returned exit N, so the result was discarded'). _backend_not_ready names the condition (WSL not installed or running; RepeatMasker not installed; Dfam root and curated libraries not both installed; FamDB could not open the library) and points to the Backend installer; custom-library genome runs skip the Dfam conditions. genome_scan's cached-genome checksum probe now has a 1800 s ceiling (was 30 s; covers a 25 GB target at 15 MB/s) and genome_prepare's tool probe is guarded: a slow WSL gives 'checking the cached genome's checksum timed out after 1800 s ... try again' instead of a raw TimeoutExpired.
records.trigger: WSL shut down mid-run, crashes, or an unready backend.
affected_outputs: annotate.ok / error text; no sealed zero-hit result from a dead session

parameters.basis: bounded by the slowest plausible read of a large target; WSL liveness is probed first

records.title: Splice detection takes the gene strand from minimap2's ts tag; minus-strand exon FASTA is numbered in transcript order
records.before: The strand was the SAM FLAG-16 orientation of the read, so an antisense read (3' ESTs, first-strand cDNA, a reverse-complemented transcript) was reported as the opposite gene strand and its splice motifs were read on the wrong strand: CT..AC instead of GT..AG, 0 canonical introns.
records.after: The gene strand combines the alignment orientation with the ts:A tag (minimap2 -x splice reports the transcript strand relative to the read): strand = alignment strand, flipped when ts is '-'. The result also returns alignment_strand, transcript_strand and strand_determined (False when no ts tag is present; the strand then falls back to the alignment strand). The splice panel states 'strand undetermined' in that case and shows alignment orientation and transcript strand separately. Exon and intron blocks and the canonical set (GT-AG, GC-AG, AT-AC) are unchanged. Exports: splice exon FASTA is sorted in transcript order (exon_1 is the mRNA's 5' exon for a minus-strand gene) with transcript_rank= and coordinate_system=0-based-half-open in the header; ORF, domain and exon FASTA headers state the convention and write a missing Pfam as NA.
records.trigger: Transcripts that align to the reverse strand or are antisense; every splice result gains the new fields.
affected_outputs: introns[].canonical and canonical_introns (counted on the corrected strand)
splice GFF/FASTA exports that carry strand

records.title: Accession validation: NZ_ accessions accepted; protein and assembly accessions get specific refusals
records.before: ACC_RE was ^[A-Za-z]{1,6}_?\d+(\.\d+)?$, so NZ_CP012345.1 was refused; protein (NP_, XP_, YP_, WP_, AP_, ZP_) and assembly (GCF_, GCA_) accessions matched the pattern and went to NCBI as nucleotide requests; the refusal example was 'M11240, NC_003075.7' (an 18.6-Mb chromosome).
records.after: ACC_RE accepts an optional upper-case NZ_ prefix; protein prefixes are refused with 'is a protein accession - TEagle fetches nucleotide records (e.g. X04456)' and GCF_/GCA_ with 'is an assembly accession, not a sequence record - use Fetch by coordinate'; the generic refusal example is 'X04456, AB087615'.
records.trigger: Typed accessions with an NZ_ prefix, protein accessions, assembly accessions.

parameters.name: accepted accession grammar
parameters.basis: RefSeq WGS/plasmid accessions; protein and assembly records are not nucleotide records

records.measured: Run in this audit (fetch.validate_accession): 'NZ_CP012345.1' refused in 4.0.0, accepted in 4.1.0; 'GCF_000001405.40' accepted in 4.0.0 (would be sent as a nucleotide id), refused in 4.1.0 with the assembly message; 'NP_000509.1' accepted in 4.0.0, refused in 4.1.0; X04456, M11240.1 and NC_003075.7 accepted in both; bare 'NZ_' and 'not!an!acc' refused in both (new example text).

A syntactically valid accession can still be absent at NCBI.
