records.title: Fetch uses the resolved accession.version; ENA headers are rewritten; unversioned and ENA-served records keep fetched provenance
records.before: retrieve() fetched the FASTA with the text the user typed and built endpoint and sourceUrl from it. A typed unversioned accession (X04456, M11240) produced a source context that did not match the verified accession.version, and an ENA-served record kept the header '>ENA|acc|acc.ver ...': in both cases normalize_source_context returned local_input, so the sealed manifest lost accession, taxon and source URL.
records.after: retrieve() fetches with the NCBI-resolved accession.version from NCBI or ENA alike, rewrites an ENA header to '>acc.ver ...' only when its third field equals that accession (otherwise untouched, so the record stays local_input), and builds endpoint and sourceUrl from the versioned accession (a cache written from the typed text is repaired on read). provenance accepts a source URL or ENA endpoint built from the typed unversioned form of the resolved accession and always emits the canonical versioned URL; URLs naming another record, version or host and headers naming another accession still downgrade to local_input.
records.trigger: Accessions typed without a version; any record served by the ENA fallback (NCBI efetch failure).
affected_outputs: input.accession, taxid, source, sourceUrl and endpoint in the manifest
FASTA header of an ENA-served record: '>ENA|X|X.1 ...' -> '>X.1 ...'
labels_renamed: inputType 'local_input' -> 'fetched_accession' for unversioned and ENA-served fetches
records.measured: Run in this audit with real engine/fetch code and a mocked network layer (canned esummary and FASTA bodies for M11240.1; refresh True; the shared on-disk cache was not touched). Typed 'M11240.1', NCBI: fetched_accession in both versions. Typed 'M11240', NCBI-served: 4.0.0 manifest inputType local_input, accession absent, identitySource local_input; 4.1.0 fetched_accession, accession M11240.1, validated_fetch, versioned sourceUrl. ENA-served (typed with or without version): 4.0.0 local_input (header '>ENA|M11240|M11240.1 desc'); 4.1.0 fetched_accession, header rewritten to '>M11240.1 desc', endpoint https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/api/fasta/M11240.1.
limitations: Both code versions share the same on-disk fetch cache; a 4.1.0 run rewrites legacy entries on read, so a 4.0.0 run after a 4.1.0 run can see a repaired cache entry.
An ENA record whose third header field names a different accession stays local_input by design.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: fetch M11240 (typed without a version; resolves to M11240.1) and run the analysis: 4.0.0 seals local_input, 4.1.0 seals fetched_accession with taxon 7227 and the versioned NCBI URL. Negative: type M11240.1: identical in both. Boundary: force the ENA fallback (NCBI blocked) for X01005: header rewritten and provenance fetched in 4.1.0, local_input in 4.0.0.
records.changelog_line: Multi-region coordinate fetches can be analysed; unversioned and ENA-served accessions keep their fetched provenance; NZ_ accessions are accepted.

records.title: Fetched gene models: absent codon_start means frame 1, introns only within one feature or gene, derived exons and introns flagged, stale caches rebuilt
records.before: A CDS without codon_start got phase None (GFF3 export failed); introns were the gaps between all exons of a record, so separate CDS features or genes gave an intergenic 'intron'; derived introns had no derived flag; derived exons inherited cds_group/phase; complete_gene_model re-derived gaps globally (quadratic).
records.after: Absent codon_start gives phase 0 (running phase for later segments); a present invalid value (empty, 0, 4, x) still gives None and the GFF3 writer fails closed. Introns are derived only within one unit (one CDS/mRNA feature, or explicit exons grouped by gene/locus_tag/transcript_id plus strand) and carry derived=True (GFF3 derived=true, BED |derived=true, FASTA ' derived=true'); derived exons drop cds_group/phase; complete_gene_model splits derived introns around synthesised exons (bisect index). GENE_MODEL_VERSION 2 stamps the cache: older models are rebuilt once; a failed feature fetch is stored as featuresStatus 'failed' and retried on the next cache hit.
records.trigger: Any fetched accession with a feature table (CDS, mRNA, exon, intron features); GFF3/BED export of a fetched gene model.

parameters.name: GENE_MODEL_VERSION
parameters.basis: forces rebuild of cached models built by the old logic

parameters.name: codon_start default
parameters.basis: INSDC feature-table convention

records.measured: Run in this audit (fetch.build_gene_model on synthetic feature lists): one CDS feature joining 10-100 and 200-301, no codon_start: 4.0.0 phases [None, None], intron 100-200 without a derived flag; 4.1.0 phases [0, 0], the same intron with derived True. Two single-interval CDS features of different genes (10-100 and 400-600): 4.0.0 one intron 100-400; 4.1.0 none (counts introns 1 -> 0).
limitations: Records that annotate separate CDS features of one transcript without a joined mRNA get no introns even where biology implies them.
Exon and intron counts of fetched records change, so any benchmark that scores fetched gene models must be rebuilt.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: fetch a multi-CDS record such as M80343 (L1.2, two ORF CDS features) and read the gene model: 4.0.0 reports a derived 'intron' between ORF1 and ORF2, 4.1.0 none. Negative: a record with a single joined CDS (for example the insulin example used for splice) keeps its intron in both, flagged derived in 4.1.0. Boundary: codon_start absent vs '2': phase 0 vs 1.
records.changelog_line: Fetched gene models export to GFF3 when the feature table omits codon_start, no introns are invented between separate CDS features or genes, and spliced CDS segments export as one feature.

records.title: Results for a previous specimen are discarded; a slow fetch cannot overwrite a later sequence; a fetch can be cancelled
records.before: A late family-annotation, splice, primer-design, in-silico-PCR or genome-scan result from a previous specimen was shown as current; a slow accession or coordinate fetch could overwrite a sequence pasted, uploaded or loaded after it; a failed fetch erased the loaded specimen's label and genome binding; there was no way to cancel a fetch.
records.after: Requests are tagged '<op>#n' with the analysis generation and settled in _retire; a result whose specimen changed is dropped and busy buttons reset; both fetch types share _start_fetch (key 'fetch#n'), any specimen change retires a pending fetch so its result is ignored, and a Cancel button appears while a fetch runs; a failed, cancelled or superseded fetch only clears the 'fetching...' indicator and restores the prior label.
records.trigger: GUI use with slow networks or quick specimen changes.
affected_outputs: which result is displayed; no engine output changes
records.measured: From tests (GUI-only).
limitations: A cancelled fetch still completes on the network; its result is ignored.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive (GUI): start a coordinate fetch, paste another sequence before it returns: 4.0.0 replaces the paste, 4.1.0 keeps it. Negative: no interleaving: identical. Boundary: cancel then fetch again.
records.changelog_line: Results of a family annotation, splice alignment, primer design, in-silico PCR or genome scan for a previous specimen are discarded instead of being shown as current, and a slow fetch can no longer overwrite a sequence entered afterwards; a Cancel button for a running accession or coordinate fetch.

records.title: A product must be longer than the longer annealed primer core (crossed 3' ends and primer-length self-primed products are no longer reported)
records.before: A pair of binding sites formed a product whenever left < right and prod_min <= templated span + tails <= prod_max. With prod_min 1, crossed 3' ends gave 15-bp 'products' shorter than a primer, a tailed crossed pair was rescued by its tails, and a palindromic 20-mer gave a 20-bp F+F product.
records.after: The pair must satisfy right - left > max(forward anneal_len, reverse anneal_len) (strict) in addition to the unchanged size window, so the two annealed cores cannot cross or coincide and no product is shorter than a primer core. Valid overlapping non-crossed pairs (for example a 30-bp span with 20-nt cores) are still reported.
records.trigger: Short product windows (prod_min below about 2 x primer length), primers that are palindromic or self-complementary at their 3' ends, and pairs that bind nearly the same position.
affected_outputs: result.amplicons: fewer products (those with right - left <= longer anneal_len are removed)
gel lanes and verdicts that counted such a product

parameters.name: product acceptance rule
parameters.v4_0_0: left < right and prod_min <= length <= prod_max
parameters.v4_1_0: right - left > max(anneal_len F, anneal_len R) and prod_min <= length <= prod_max
parameters.basis: a product shorter than a primer core cannot be a PCR product

parameters.name: prod_min / prod_max defaults (run_pcr)
parameters.basis: unchanged

records.measured: Run in this audit with primers.in_silico_pcr on M11240 (prod_min 1, prod_max 1000, max_mm 2, tp 5, min_anneal 18). Crossed ends (F = bases 100-120, R = reverse complement of bases 95-115): 4.0.0 reports two 15-bp F+R products (100-115 and a second site at 4970-4985 in the 3' LTR copy); 4.1.0 reports none. Palindromic 20-mer (ACGT)5 inserted at 500 as a primer: 4.0.0 F+F products of 20, 24, 24 and 28 bp; 4.1.0 24, 24 and 28 bp (the 20-bp product is dropped, the 24-bp ones carry 2 permitted mismatches). A normal 320-bp pair at 1000-1320 is identical in both.
limitations: The 4.0.0 default prod_min is 70, so the change matters only for short windows or for self-primed palindromic primers; most benchmark runs at defaults see no difference.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: F = M11240[100:120], R = revcomp(M11240[95:115]) at prod_min 1: 4.0.0 gives 15-bp products, 4.1.0 none. Negative: F = M11240[1000:1020], R = revcomp(M11240[1300:1320]): one 320-bp product in both. Boundary: palindromic (ACGT)5 as both primers: product lengths 20 (dropped in 4.1.0), 21 (kept) when anneal_len is 20.
records.changelog_line: In-silico PCR takes each primer's annealing core from the specimen ...; products shorter than the annealed cores are no longer reported, and a template ambiguity code always counts as a mismatch.

records.title: A template ambiguity code always counts as a mismatch, including against an identical primer code
records.before: _base_ok returned True when the primer base equalled the template base, so primer N matched template N and primer R matched template R at zero cost; a degenerate primer base otherwise matched any template base it covers.
records.after: A primer base matches only when its IUPAC set contains the template base and that base is A, C, G or T; an ambiguous or unknown template base (N, R, Y, ...) is a mismatch whatever the primer base. The degenerate-primer table and the rest of the matcher are unchanged.
records.trigger: Templates with N or IUPAC codes at a primer footprint (assembly gaps, consensus sequences) searched with primers that carry the same code.
affected_outputs: fwd_mm / rev_mm of products across an ambiguous template base (+1 per such base)
products that exceed max_mm after the extra mismatch disappear

parameters.name: max_mm default
parameters.basis: unchanged

parameters.name: tp (strict 3' window)
parameters.basis: unchanged

records.measured: Run in this audit on M11240 with a template N (and R) planted at 1010 inside the forward primer site and the primer carrying the same code: max_mm 0 -> 4.0.0 one product with fwd_mm 0, 4.1.0 none (also for R vs R); max_mm 2 -> 4.0.0 fwd_mm 0, 4.1.0 fwd_mm 1 for the same product.

Negative: same template, primer with the real base: identical. records.title: Primer input is normalised (whitespace, case, U to T) and anything outside the IUPAC codes is rejected
records.before: in_silico_pcr only upper-cased the primers; a space inside a primer silently gave zero products (status complete_zero_products), '-', '1' or letters outside IUPAC did not raise, and RNA 'U' primers were sealed unnormalised. run_pcr gated primers with the generic _require_nt check.
records.after: primers.normalize_primer strips all whitespace, upper-cases, reads U as T and raises ValueError naming the offending characters ('forward primer contains characters that are not IUPAC nucleotide codes: ...'); run_pcr applies it before matching, the design-provenance comparison and sealing (BadRequest on error); in_silico_pcr applies the same step. The genome-scan route does not use it (see unchanged).
records.trigger: Pasted or typed primers containing spaces, lower case, U, digits or gap characters.
affected_outputs: products for a primer with an internal space: none -> normal product
error instead of silent zero products for illegal characters
sealed primer sequences are the normalised DNA text

parameters.v4_0_0: run_pcr: nucleotide-ish by _require_nt; in_silico_pcr: any upper-cased text
parameters.v4_1_0: ACGTRYSWKMBDHVN after stripping whitespace and U->T
parameters.basis: IUPAC nucleotide codes

records.measured: Run in this audit on M11240 (primers.in_silico_pcr): a space inside the forward primer returns [] in 4.0.0 and the normal 320-bp product in 4.1.0; a '-' returns [] in 4.0.0 and raises 'forward primer contains characters that are not IUPAC nucleotide codes: '-'' in 4.1.0; lower-case and U primers give the same product in both.
limitations: Primer minimum length (18) and the 5' tail rule are enforced elsewhere (engine and panel).
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: forward primer with an embedded space: 4.0.0 zero products, 4.1.0 one. Negative: clean upper-case primers identical. Boundary: a primer with 'U' is read as T in both matchers, but only 4.1.0 seals the T form.
records.changelog_line: missing from CHANGELOG

records.title: Annealing cores are taken from the specimen and applied to background sequences
records.before: Every sequence (specimen and each custom background) was searched alone: per primer and strand, only the sites that reach the longest 3'-proximal core found in that sequence were kept, and the core was reported as anneal_len with the 5' remainder as tail. Results carried no record of the cores used.
records.after: When backgrounds are supplied, run_pcr derives each primer's per-strand core from the specimen alone (primers.specimen_cores) and passes it to the backgrounds: in a background, best = min(its own longest reach, the specimen core) and every site reaching at least that length is kept and called at it. The specimen (k = 0) is always searched as a lone search, so its result no longer depends on the backgrounds. A strand where the specimen has no site gives core None and the background keeps its own. criteria.annealing_core reports the cores used (the largest per primer and strand over the searched sequences).
records.trigger: In-silico PCR with a custom background where the specimen's best site for a primer is shorter than a site in the background (an imperfect specimen copy against a perfect background copy).
affected_outputs: background amplicons: perfect sites re-called with shorter anneal_len and a tail (anneal 26 -> 20, tail 0 -> 6, start shifted by the tail length, product_length unchanged)
background amplicons: additional products from sites between the specimen core and the background's own best reach
same sequence can give different product sets as specimen and as background

parameters.name: core selection per sequence
parameters.v4_0_0: longest core reached in that sequence
parameters.v4_1_0: specimen: unchanged; background: min(own longest, specimen core)
parameters.basis: makes an identical site get the same call in specimen and background

parameters.name: min_anneal
parameters.basis: primers.MIN_PRIMER_SIZE, unchanged

records.measured: Run in this audit through engine.run_pcr; 26-mer forward and 24-mer reverse primer, max_mm 2, tp 5, synthetic random sequences (seed 7). Specimen holds only a forward-site copy with 8 mismatches in its 5' end (core 20, tail 6); background holds the perfect site plus the mismatched copy, each followed by the reverse site. 4.0.0: specimen product (anneal 20, tail 6, 2 mm) plus two background products at the perfect site (anneal 26, tail 0; 200 and 470 bp). 4.1.0: same specimen product; the two background products are re-called at anneal 20 / tail 6 with the start shifted 200 -> 206 (lengths unchanged) AND a third background product from the mismatched copy (start 506, 170 bp, anneal 20, tail 6, 2 mm) that the background's own lone search drops. A perfect specimen with the same background gives the same three products at core 26 in both versions; a background with only the mismatched copy gives the same product in both; searched alone, the background still hides the mismatched copy when a perfect site exists (2 products in both).
limitations: A perfect background site is reported with the specimen's shorter core and a tail (26-nt perfect site reads 20 + 6); tail bases are not scored.
The same sequence now gives different product sets as specimen (lone rule hides the shorter imperfect copy) and as background (both copies reported): a new asymmetry.
CHANGELOG says 'without dropping any product'; it does not say 4.1.0 can add products and re-call perfect sites.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: specimen with only an imperfect primer site, background with perfect + imperfect sites: 4.0.0 reports the perfect site only; 4.1.0 reports both, re-called at the specimen core. Negative: single-sequence run (no background): identical. Boundary: specimen with a perfect site: background results identical in both versions (core 26).
records.changelog_line: In-silico PCR takes each primer's annealing core from the specimen and applies it to background sequences without dropping any product a background gives on its own.

records.title: Search-cap flags are set only when something was skipped
records.before: amplicons_capped and sites_capped were set when the count reached MAX_AMPS / MAX_SITES (4000 each), so a search that found exactly 4000 products or sites was reported as truncated.
records.after: The flags are set only when a further site or product exists beyond the limit (checked before appending).
records.trigger: Searches that find exactly MAX_AMPS (4000) products or MAX_SITES (4000) sites; very rare in practice.
affected_outputs: stats.amplicons_capped / stats.sites_capped; engine truncated flag and the 'stopped early' banner

parameters.name: MAX_SITES / MAX_AMPS
parameters.basis: unchanged limits

An option is disabled when its flank is shorter than the minimum primer size (18 nt); with no terminal-repeat pair the goal says the edges are unknown; a record that ends at the element says to fetch the insertion with flank by coordinate.

records.title: LTR pair measured with a gapped alignment; identity redefined; lower-bound cause named
records.before: v4.0.0: find_ltr seeded 13-mers on the best diagonal (+/-3), then extended that single diagonal with an ungapped X-drop (+1 match, -2 mismatch, x_drop 30). Identity was matches / min(len) of the two ungapped copies (N==N never a match, but N counted in the denominator). One indel put everything downstream out of phase: a copia LTR pair with a 1-bp deletion read 75.0% (advisory 'Sub-threshold terminal direct repeat'), a 10-bp deletion truncated the LTR to the in-phase part (166 bp, 100%, span shifted by 110 bp). length_is_lower_bound was set when the repeat touched a record end or an extension stopped at its limit; bound_reason was always the single 'still matched where the record ends' sentence. Method string was always 'k-mer seed (k=13, W bp window) + X-drop diagonal extension'.
records.after: 4.1.0: the ungapped measurement is kept as a candidate. A gapped candidate is also built, and attempted only when there is no ungapped candidate, the ungapped identity is below 97.0, or seed anchors lie 4-32 diagonals from the best diagonal. The gapped candidate chains collinear anchors across diagonals up to 32 away (_chain), extends both ends with a banded affine-gap X-drop (gap open 4, extension 1, band = indel margin 8 + 4), and measures identity from one banded global alignment of the final extents (identity = matches / (matches + mismatches + gap columns); ambiguous columns excluded; skipped, leaving the ungapped result, when the band exceeds 250,000 cells). The candidate with the higher score (matches - 2 mismatches - 4 per gap event - 1 per gap column) is reported. Ungapped identity is now matches / columns where both bases are A/C/G/T. Rows from the gapped path carry indels (gap events) and a method string 'banded gapped alignment'. The lower-bound flag still fires on a record edge, and bound_reason now names the cause ('the repeat still matched where the record ends', 'the two copies met each other', or both joined by ' and'). Accepted rows then pass through _snap_ltr (STR-002).
records.trigger: Any record in which the two LTR copies differ by an indel of up to 32 bp, or whose ungapped identity is below 97%. Bare specimens whose copies are identical or substitution-only stay on the ungapped path and give the same length and identity. Records with anchors only on the best diagonal and ungapped identity at or above 97% are unaffected.

records.measured: Own run, both engines in separate processes, same seeds. M11240.1 (copia) bare: 1-bp deletion 100 bp into the 3' LTR: v4.0.0 advisory row, 276 bp, 75.0%; 4.1.0 LTR row, 276 bp, 99.6%, indels 1. 2-bp deletion: 75.7% -> 99.3%. 10-bp deletion: v4.0.0 LTR 166 bp at 100% span [110,5136]; 4.1.0 LTR 276 bp at 96.4% span [0,5136]. Synthetic pairs (300-bp random LTR, 2 kb random interior, 3' copy mutated, 20 seeds 0-19): 5% substitution + 1% indel (indels up to 3 bp): accepted 4/20 -> 20/20, length within 5% of truth 2/20 -> 20/20; 10% sub + 2% indel: 2/20 -> 20/20; 15% sub + 2% indel: 1/20 -> 19/20 (18 full length). Single deletion in a 400-bp LTR (20 seeds): full 400 bp recovered at deletion 6, 20, 31, 32 bp in 20/20 (4.1.0) versus 0/20 (v4.0.0, reports ~200 bp at 100%); at 33 and 36 bp both versions report ~200 bp. Insertion in the 3' copy: 20 and 32 bp recovered 20/20, 40 bp not. Substitution-only controls are unchanged: 300-bp LTR at 5% sub 20/20 both; 20% sub 19/20 both. Realised substitution sweep (60 seeds each, 300-bp LTR): accepted at 20% divergence 38 -> 39, at 22% 26 -> 28, 25% 8 -> 8, 28% 2 -> 2, 30% 0 -> 0 (the gapped measure moves a few pairs across the 80% floor). Bare copia M11240.1 and gypsy M12927.1: LTR 276 and 482 bp at 100.0%, unchanged. Wave record: 40 diverged pairs (4% sub + 3 indels, 500 bp) full length 4/100 -> 40/40.
limitations: Indels longer than 32 bp (deletion or insertion) still halve the LTR to the in-phase part, as in v4.0.0 (measured at 33, 36, 40, 60 bp).
The near-miss advisory row built from a gapped candidate still carries the method text 'X-drop diagonal extension' because that string is hard-coded in the rejection branch.

Gapped identity is a score-optimal alignment and is slightly optimistic for heavily diverged pairs: a copia pair with 120 bp of 3'-LTR randomised read 79.7% ungapped (v4.0.0 advisory) and 82.5% gapped (accepted, classification moves from superfamily-undetermined to Copia).
LTRs of 6 kb or more cannot be seeded (seed window 6000 bp); gapped alignment is skipped above 250,000 band cells so very long diverged pairs fall back to the ungapped measurement.

records.changelog_line: LTR identity and length are measured from a gapped alignment, so an indel between the LTR copies no longer reads as heavy divergence or halves the LTR; boundaries are refined jointly with the target-site duplication. (The lower-bound cause wording and the identity definition change are missing from CHANGELOG.)

records.title: LTR outer boundaries re-chosen jointly with the flanking TSD (boundary snapping)
records.before: v4.0.0: the LTR outer ends were wherever the X-drop extension stopped. An extension past the true end keeps a chance-matching base about a quarter of the time, so a flanked element's boundary landed 1-4 bp too wide and its real TSD was searched at the wrong place: a 5-bp TSD was typically reported as 4, 3 or 2 bp (flagged incongruent downstream) and ltr_len came out 277 or 483 instead of 276 or 482.
records.after: 4.1.0: every accepted LTR pair is passed through _snap_ltr. Over 36 shifts (5' end -1..+4, 3' end -4..+1) a shifted boundary is taken only if it gives a TSD of at least 4 bp, total evidence at least 5, and a gain of at least 1.5 over the unshifted boundary after a cost of 0.5 per base moved. Evidence is the TSD length capped at 6, plus 1 when it equals the Copia modal length (5), plus 3 when both LTR ends read canonical TG..CA. On a move the row gets new ltr_len, five_prime, three_prime, element_span, termini, boundary_adjustment [a, b], boundary_tests 36; termini.selected_for_motif is true when the canonical-motif bonus decided the move. Ungapped rows get identity recomputed; gapped rows keep the alignment identity. detect_all then searches the TSD at the snapped span with placements = boundary_tests, so the TSD chance is adjusted (STR-011).
records.trigger: Flanked records (at least 4 bp of flank on both sides) holding an accepted LTR pair whose unshifted boundary has no TSD or a shorter one than a shifted boundary offers. Bare records and records with the TSD already exact are unchanged.

records.after: 4.1.0: the floor is max(4, min(192, 0.05 * (len - 3))). Behaviour is identical below about 3,840 bp (where 0.05*(len-3) < 192) and the change matters above about 5.1 kb. Exact microsatellites remain simple (e.g. (ATTA)n and (AT)n at 6 kb).

records.title: Ambiguity codes are neither matches nor mismatches; ACGT-only TSD; input upper-cased
records.before: v4.0.0: LTR and TIR identity divided matches by the full arm length, so N and IUPAC columns counted as mismatches (only N and n excluded from the match count); the LTR X-drop extension penalised N as a mismatch and stopped at an N-run; find_tsd accepted any equal flank strings that held no 'N', so an IUPAC TSD such as ACRYT was reported as a 5-bp TSD; PBS identity counted only N/n as unknown. find_ltr, find_tir and detect_all did not upper-case their input.
records.after: 4.1.0: a column counts only when both bases are A, C, G or T. Identity is matches / known columns (LTR ungapped, TIR scan) or matches / (matches + mismatches + gap columns) with ambiguous columns excluded (gapped). The X-drop extension and the gapped alignment treat an ambiguous column as neutral, so an N-run no longer stops extension. LTR rows carry ambiguous_columns when non-zero. find_tsd (via _tsd_at) accepts only ACGT motifs. PBS identity counts a match only for A/C/G/T. find_ltr, find_tir and detect_all upper-case the sequence (the engine already normalises case, so engine results are the same for lower-case input).
records.trigger: Records containing N or IUPAC codes inside or next to a terminal repeat, a TSD or a PBS leader window; direct callers passing lower-case sequence to the detector functions.

records.title: TIR search in flanked genomic records: seeded arms, joint trimming with the TSD, boundary_uncertain
records.before: v4.0.0: find_tir first read the record ends (_terminal_tir, anchored at positions 0 and n); if that failed it seeded 11-mers within 1200 bp of each end (>= 3 anchors on one anti-diagonal), took the single densest diagonal and reported the extent of the anchor cluster (identity >= 80, not _is_simple) with no TSD test. In a flanked record the winner was often a 13-bp subterminal repeat inside the element, or an arm anchored in the flank: flanked Ac gave tir_len 13 at [element+113, element end-82], TSD absent. Short or imperfect TIRs (hAT 11 bp at 90.9%) had no 11-mer seed and were not found.
records.after: 4.1.0: the anchored read of the record ends is tried first and returns as in v4.0.0 (a chance repeat at the ends of a flanked record can stand in for the real one, about 1% of the time). Otherwise two seeded searches run, one candidate per diagonal: (a) exact 11-mers (>= 3 clustered on a diagonal, i.e. a ~13-bp perfect core) within 1200 bp of each end, arms measured up to 1000 bp; (b) exact 6-mers (>= 2 on a diagonal) within 400 bp of each end, arms measured up to 60 bp. Each diagonal is walked outward (X-drop 6), cut of any tandem run (STR-009), then scanned with an identity-aware X-drop of 60. For every candidate the arm pair is re-placed jointly with the TSD over shifts from -2 to +6 (trim at most 6 inward, restore at most 2 outward) using _snap_choice with a 5-bp minimum. A candidate is accepted when it is 'supported' (a flanking TSD of at least 6 bp that is not inside a microsatellite) or 'strong' (an exact core of at least 13 bp). Supported candidates have their arms re-measured at 90% identity (in place of the 80% floor); unsupported ones are reported as their exact core. Candidates are ranked by (supported and core at least 20 bp, core at least 20 bp, supported, TSD length, strong, length), so a corroborated terminus outranks a longer subterminal repeat. Rows carry boundary_adjustment [a,-a] when trimmed, boundary_tests when TSD-supported, and boundary_uncertain=true when not. The method string gains the window ('k-mer seed vs reverse-complement (k=11, 1200 bp window)'). length_is_lower_bound is set only when the arm reached the scan limit.
records.trigger: Records that have flank on both sides of a TIR element (any genomic window), where the anchored read of the record ends finds nothing; TIR elements with a 6-bp or longer TSD benefit most. Bare elements (the record starts and ends on the element) are unchanged.

records.measured: Own run: X05424.1 (Ac) with 300-bp random flanks and a random 8-bp TSD, 30 seeds: exact span plus TSD 0/30 (v4.0.0, reports 13-bp subterminal TIR) -> 25/30. 10 seeds per flank length, TSD 8: exact 10/10 at flank 300, 350, 380 and 0/10 at 400, 450, 600 (joint window); v4.0.0 0/10 everywhere. A TSD shorter than 6 bp can never corroborate: families with 2-4 bp TSDs (Tc1/Mariner TA, piggyBac TTAA, and 3-bp CACTA or PIF/Harbinger in typical descriptions) are reported only as an uncorroborated exact core (STR-006) unless classification recovers the target site (STR-007).

With no TSD, the 13-bp subterminal repeat still outranks the 11-bp Ac terminus: Ac with 300-bp flanks and no TSD gives tir_len 13 at element offset +113 in both versions, now flagged boundary_uncertain.
A chance inverted repeat at the very ends of a flanked record is read by the anchored path and can stand in for the real TIR (about 1%).
A 12-bp (TA)6 'TSD' inside a flanking (TA)n run is still emitted by detect_all with chance_level false (the microsatellite-TSD guard acts only on corroboration inside the TIR ranking).
Chance TIR rows on random 4-kb records rose slightly (1 -> 3 per 200 at 50% GC), all below 20 bp and flagged boundary_uncertain.

records.title: Uncorroborated flanked TIR candidates reported as their exact core: long imperfect arms are shortened
records.before: v4.0.0: in a flanked record a seeded TIR candidate was reported with the extent of its anchor cluster whether or not a TSD supported it. A flanked 60-bp arm with 10% mismatches came back near 53 bp (median) and a 200-bp arm with 10% mismatches near 186 bp, with start offsets of about 1 bp from the true end in most records. tsd_state read 'absent (flanks present, no direct repeat found)'.
records.after: 4.1.0: a candidate with no TSD of 6 bp or longer is accepted only if it has an exact core of at least 13 bp, and is then reported as that exact core, never as an extended arm, so that a seeded search over a long flank cannot reach 20+ bp by chance (MIN_TIR_STANDALONE). The row has boundary_uncertain=true and the TSD search is not run against its boundary: tsd_state is 'not assessed (element boundary uncertain: the repeat arms were placed by repeat strength alone)'. Cores shorter than min_tir (10) are not reported. With a TSD of 6 bp or more the arms are extended and measured at 90% identity.
records.trigger: Flanked records whose TIR element has no flanking TSD of at least 6 bp, i.e. (a) no TSD planted or lost, and (b) superfamilies with TSDs shorter than 6 bp, notably Tc1/Mariner TA, piggyBac TTAA, CACTA and PIF/Harbinger (3 bp in typical descriptions), unless a superfamily call later recovers the site (STR-007). Long imperfect arms (MULE/Foldback-like) are affected most.

records.title: Microsatellite arm and microsatellite-TSD guards for TIR candidates (periods 1-6, self-paired units)
records.before: v4.0.0: a TIR candidate was rejected only if its 5' arm was _is_simple (fewer distinct 4-mers than the floor). A diverged tandem repeat passes that test: a 35-bp (TA)n arm with one substitution, a 10-bp CTGCAGCAGC arm, and (AATT)n, (GATC)n, (ACGT)n arrays all pair with their own reverse complement, so they were reported as TIRs (arms up to the 1-kb limit) and classified 'non-autonomous TIR element'; a TSD formed by the run also counted.
records.after: 4.1.0: _simple_arms rejects a candidate when the 5' arm is _is_simple, or when any of six windows (5' arm, 3' arm, each arm with 16 bp outside it, each arm with 16 bp inside it) is a tandem run by _period_run. _period_run tests periods 1-2 for windows under 20 bp and periods 1-6 from 20 bp, allowing at most 15% broken comparisons (30% from 20 bp); a period-4-6 reading counts only when its unit is its own reverse complement up to rotation (GATC, AATT, AAATTT) or repeats a unit of period 1-3, so a unit that cannot pair with itself, such as the Ginger1-type (TCTA)n terminal repeat, is kept. _tsd_in_microsatellite zeroes a candidate's TSD when a TSD of 6 bp or more lies in a tandem run (any unit, period 1-6) that continues 8 bp outside it, so it cannot corroborate. The same guard applies on the anchored path (_scan_tir) and on every seeded path.
records.trigger: Records holding or flanked by microsatellite or minisatellite arrays (including diverged ones up to about 10%), and elements whose terminal repeat begins with a self-paired run.
affected_outputs: TIR rows disappear for such arrays and flanks
classification: 'non-autonomous TIR element' 31 -> 0-1 on diverged arrays
TIR row arms no longer extended through a flanking microsatellite
tsd_state/TSD corroboration for candidates whose TSD is a run

False rejection of random windows by _period_run, GC 0.5 / 0.35 / 0.2: 10 bp 0.04% / 0.12% / 0.67%; 20 bp 0.08% / 0.17% / 1.56%; of a real random arm by _simple_arms with 16 bp random sides: 10 bp 0.25% (GC 0.5), 0.73% (GC 0.35), 4.31% (GC 0.2). A microsatellite arm at the far ends of a flanking region of two different non-pairing runs, e.g. (CA)n on one side and (TG)n on the other, still extends the arms into the runs.
Tolerances and the 16-bp inside window are inline literals and are not sealed.

records.title: Tandem run cut from TIR arms instead of discarding the candidate (transposon inserted next to a (TA)n run)
records.before: v4.0.0: the seeded TIR arms ran outward through the target site into an adjacent (TA)n run, which pairs with the other half of a split run, so a Tc1 inserted at TA next to a run reported arms of 75, 115 or 154 bp for runs of 20, 60 and 100 bp, element_span widened to include part of each run, and no TSD.
records.after: 4.1.0: after the outward walk each seeded candidate has its outer ends read as a tandem run of period 1-6 (+1/-2 comparison walk, X-drop 14, started up to 40 bp outside the arm, run allowed to start within 10 bp of the arm end, smallest period within 90% of the best score, net score 10 or more). If the run's unit is its own reverse complement up to rotation (self-paired: TA, GATC, AATT) it is cut from both ends (the longer of the two sides), arms are then measured on the trimmed span and checked with reach 0. A run that fills 1 kb (max_tir) or half the span drops the candidate. A run of an unpaired unit (A(n), (CA)n) at both arm ends is treated as the element's own.
records.trigger: Flanked records in which the element sits next to a self-paired tandem run of net score 10 or more at the arm end: Tc1/Mariner next to (TA)n is the realistic case.
affected_outputs: TIR row tir_len, element_span (back to the true arm, e.g. 54 bp for Tc1)
TSD row presence (TA or the run-derived TSD), tsd_state
classification confidence for Tc1 next to a run (Candidate returns to Moderate)

records.title: TSD rows carry a composition-adjusted chance probability; chance_level flag; ACGT-only TSD
records.before: v4.0.0: a TSD row had type, length, motif, upstream, downstream and matched_expected only. A 2-bp match and a 12-bp match were indistinguishable by any reported number; any equal flank strings without N were accepted.
records.after: 4.1.0: find_tsd(placements=1) adds chance_probability, n_tests and chance_level. chance_probability = 1 - [prod over lengths l from L to max_tsd of (1 - (sum of squared base frequencies of the whole record)^l)]^placements, with a single length when the expected length matched first; n_tests = lengths x placements; chance_level = chance_probability > CHANCE_LEVEL_P (1e-3). placements is 1 for a fixed span, boundary_tests for a snapped LTR or a TSD-corroborated TIR, and trim + 1 for the palindromic target-site recovery. At uniform composition chance_level is true for TSDs of 2-5 bp (e.g. 0.085, 0.023, 0.0061, 0.0014 for 2, 3, 4, 5 bp when searched without an expected length) and false from 6 bp (0.00037); AT-rich records read higher. Classification no longer says the insertion site is captured unless chance_level is false (a row without the field is treated as chance level).
records.trigger: Every TSD row. The chance_level flag affects wording and scoring wherever a consumer reads it.
affected_outputs: TSD row new keys chance_probability, n_tests, chance_level
'insertion site captured' wording in the TIR evidence (classify)
TSD row absence for IUPAC-only matches

parameters.basis: new; a single pre-specified 5-bp match is 9.8e-4 at uniform composition; unspecified-length matches and snapped boundaries need more

records.measured: Own run, find_tsd on random flanks with an exact planted TSD (seed = length; 60-bp random pads; ~uniform composition): chance_probability / chance_level / n_tests for L = 2: 0.0852 / true / 11; 3: 0.0226 / true / 10; 4: 0.0061 / true / 9; 5: 0.00142 / true / 8 (expect=5: 0.00106 / true); 6: 0.000368 / false / 7; 8: 2.1e-05 / false / 5; 12: 6.5e-08 / false / 1. Engine on flanked specimens (300-bp random flanks): copia and gypsy 5-bp TSD chance_level true (p 0.00212 in detect_all); Ac 8-bp false (5.7e-4); L1.2 12-bp false (5.4e-4); Tc1 2-bp true (0.18). Random 4-kb records, seeds 1000-1199: 1 TSD row at 50% GC and 1 at 35% GC, none non-chance.
limitations: Every genuine 4-6 bp LTR TSD and every 2-bp Tc1/Mariner TA reads chance_level true; only 6 bp or longer reads false. A scorer that counts 'TSD found' as chance_level == false will count true positives as failures.

The chance model uses whole-record base composition and assumes independent bases, so a TSD inside a tandem run is scored as extremely unlikely: a 12-bp (TA)6 flank inside a (TA)n run gets chance 1e-7 and chance_level false (copia between (TA)30 runs: 2.4e-07).
The 1e-3 level is applied per search, not corrected across the records of a run.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: M11240.1 flanked with a random 5-bp TSD (300-bp random flanks): v4.0.0 TSD row without chance fields; 4.1.0 chance_probability ~2e-3, chance_level true, n_tests 8. Same with a 12-bp TSD (L1.2 M80343.1 construct): chance ~5e-4, false. Negative: random 4-kb record at 50% GC: no TSD row with chance_level false. Boundary: TSD length 5 (true) versus 6 (false) at uniform composition; (TA)n flank run of 12 bp (chance_level false although the repeat is uninformative).
records.changelog_line: Target-site duplication rows carry a chance probability adjusted for every length and boundary placement searched, and structural rows carry their TSD state (found, absent, partially assessable, not assessable, not assessed).

records.title: TSD congruence uses superfamily length ranges and a required motif
records.before: v4.0.0: TSD_EXPECT mapped a superfamily to one length (Copia 5, Gypsy 5, hAT 8, Tc1/Mariner 2) and a TSD was congruent only at exactly that length; any 2-bp match was congruent for Tc1/Mariner; tsd_congruence took no motif.
records.after: 4.1.0: TSD_EXPECT holds (preferred length, accepted range, basis, required motif): Copia and Gypsy 5 (accepted 4-6 bp; Wicker et al. 2007, Ou et al. 2019), hAT 8 (8-8), Tc1/Mariner 2 (2-2, motif TA). tsd_congruence(length, superfamily, motif=None) returns congruent when the length is inside the range, adds expected_range, and when a motif is supplied and a motif is required it returns incongruent unless the motif matches (expected_motif/observed_motif). The preferred length 'expected' is unchanged and still drives find_tsd(expect=) in classification. 'Not diagnostic' superfamilies and 'not assessed' (length None) are unchanged. classify passes the motif and quotes range and motif in the wording; its incongruent sentence no longer says 'likely coincidental'.
records.trigger: Any LTR or Tc1/Mariner/hAT classification with a TSD.

verdict for non-TA 2-bp TSD on Tc1/Mariner: congruent -> incongruent (when the motif is passed)

records.title: Poly-A tail detection: A-rich tract with interruptions and a 3-bp end slack
records.before: v4.0.0: find_polya counted the run of A's that reached the last base of the record (>= 8) as the 3' tail, and the run of T's that began at the first base (>= 8) as the 5' poly-T. A single non-A base, or any 1-3 bases after the tail, ended the run and the tail was missed or truncated (L1.2 tail with one G: 13 bp instead of 27).
records.after: 4.1.0: the tail is the best-scoring A-rich tract (A +1, any other base -9, about one interruption per ten bases at the floor; the tract starts and ends on an A) in the last 600 bp, with at least 8 A's; it counts when it ends within 3 bases of the record end. The row length is the tract span (interruptions included), not the A count. Only the 3'-most qualifying tail is returned. The 5' poly-T of a reverse-oriented element is found by the same search on the reverse complement. find_polya still returns the row list; min_run (8) now counts A's in the tract.
records.trigger: Records whose tail has a non-A interruption or 1-3 bases after it; bare tails that are a clean homopolymer at the end give the same row.
affected_outputs: poly-A tail (3') row length and pos
classification credit for a tail (LINE confidence)

records.title: Poly-A tail corroborated by a flanking TSD anywhere in the last 600 bp, with family-wise chance control
records.before: v4.0.0: a tail followed by flank (a genomic window) was never found, so a flanked LINE had no tail row and no target-site duplication; classification fell to Candidate (flanked L1.2 + 12-bp TSD + 300-bp flanks: 0/60).
records.after: 4.1.0: a tail that does not end within 3 bases of the record end counts when it is followed by a direct repeat of at least 8 bp of the sequence before the element (the TPRT target-site duplication). The repeat is searched from 12 bp down to 8 bp, left copy within the first 600 bp of the record, the tail end tried at each of the last few A positions (longest duplication wins). It is accepted only if its family-wise chance, 1 - (1 - p)^n_tests with p from the record's composition and n_tests = tail ends tried x left-copy positions x flanked tracts, is at most 1e-3. The row gets tsd_corroborated=true, and the TSD is emitted as a TSD row (context 'flanks a poly-A tail (target-primed reverse transcription)', matched_expected false, chance_probability, n_tests, chance_level) only when no LTR or TIR row exists. The mirror search on the reverse complement gives the poly-T row and its TSD.
records.trigger: Flanked records of non-LTR, non-TIR elements (LINEs) with a TSD of about 11-12 bp or longer and flanks of up to roughly 590 bp on the left and 600 bp on the right.

records.measured: Own run: M80343.1 + 12-bp random TSD + 300-bp random flanks, 30 seeds: tail row 0 -> 30, TSD row 0 -> 30, exact (tail end and 12-bp TSD at the true positions) 0 -> 29. Engine, seeds 3 and 4: 'LINE (non-LTR)' Candidate -> Moderate with poly-A 27 bp at [6335,6362] and a 12-bp TSD (chance 5.4e-4, chance_level false). 10-seed flank sweep: recovered 10/10 at left flank 100, 300, 590 (right 300) and at right flank 500; 0/10 at left flank 700 and at right flank 700, in both orientations (poly-T mirrored). TSD length (20 seeds, 20-A tail, 300-bp flanks, 1.5-kb random body): 12 bp 20/20, 8 bp 0/20, 6 bp 0/20 in both versions. Flank composition: 12-bp TSD with flank GC 0.50 / 0.35 / 0.30: 20/20, 20/20, 19/20 (the chance term uses the whole-record composition, here dominated by the L1 body). Controls: an internal A14 run in random flanks: no tail in either version; wave record: credited tails in 400 records without a planted TSD, with an internal A14 run, 16/400 and 43/400 (intermediate build) -> 0/400; recall for planted TSD of 8/10/11/12/15 bp at 50% GC: 3/59/99/100/100%.
limitations: Only a TSD of about 11-12 bp or longer corroborates; the search is capped at MAX_TSD 12, so an 8-10 bp LINE TSD is not credited (0/20 at 8 bp).
The left copy must start within the first 600 bases of the record and the tail within the last 600: a left flank over about 590 bp or a right flank over 600 bp hides the tail.
The family-wise test uses whole-record composition: a record that is AT-rich overall (not only its flanks, about 30% GC or lower) cannot corroborate even a perfect 12-mer.
The TSD framing a tail is emitted only when there is no LTR or TIR row.
The test is per strand; a record searched on both strands carries up to about twice the per-strand false rate (0/400 measured per record).
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: M80343.1 with a random 12-bp TSD on both sides and 300-bp random flanks, 30 seeds. v4.0.0: no poly-A row, no TSD row, classification Candidate; 4.1.0: poly-A 27 bp ending at the TSD, TSD 12 bp with chance_level false, Moderate. Negative: random flanks of 300 bp around a body with an internal A14 run and no TSD: no tail in either version; the same with an 8-bp TSD: no tail in either. Boundary: left flank 590 bp (found) versus 700 bp (not found); TSD 12 bp (found) versus 10-11 bp (marginal) versus 8 bp (not found).
records.changelog_line: Terminal inverted repeats are located in records that carry genomic flanks, ...; poly-A tails followed by flank or interrupted by one base are found, with chance tails controlled for multiple testing.

records.title: LTR cis-elements (PBS, PPT, poly(A) signal) read on the element's own strand; orientation from cis-elements or the domain strand
records.before: v4.0.0: PBS, PPT and the poly(A) signal were always searched on the forward strand of the record, with no strand field and no statement of orientation. A reverse-complemented copia lost its PPT and reported an antisense poly(A) signal in the wrong LTR; forward searches on a record of unknown orientation produced chance rows.
records.after: 4.1.0: detect_all(seq, orientation=None) reads the cis-elements per orientation. A caller-supplied '+' or '-' is used as given; otherwise both strands are read and the one with more evidence wins, evidence being a PPT row, a confident PBS (>= 72%), or a poly(A) signal with its downstream element found; on a tie (including no evidence) the three rows are withheld and the LTR row carries cis_orientation 'undetermined' and cis_note. On '-' the detectors run on the reverse complement and are mapped back to record coordinates. Rows carry strand '+' or '-'; the accepted LTR row carries cis_orientation, cis_orientation_source ('caller' or 'cis-elements') and pbs_scope. In engine.analyze, when the LTR row is 'undetermined' after the domain scan and every RT/INT/TPase hit shares a strand, detect_all is re-run with that strand and the LTR row gets cis_orientation_source 'domain-strand'; an orientation already set by cis-elements is never overridden. find_ppt and find_polya_signal are unchanged (AST-identical) but now run on strand-specific sequence.
records.trigger: Every record with an accepted LTR row. Reverse-oriented elements and elements with no clear PPT/PBS/PAS evidence change most.

LTR row new keys cis_orientation, cis_orientation_source, cis_note, pbs_scope
PPT/PAS rows on reverse-oriented elements (previously missing or on the wrong strand)
PBS/PPT/PAS rows withheld when the orientation is undetermined

records.measured: Own run: forward M11240.1 and M12927.1: PPT [4861,4870] / [6976,6987] and poly(A) signal [4954,4960] / [7138,7144] identical to v4.0.0 plus strand '+', LTR row cis_orientation '+', source 'cis-elements'. Reverse complement of M11240.1: v4.0.0 only an antisense polyA-signal at [4902,4908], no PPT; 4.1.0 PPT [276,285] strand '-' and polyA-signal [186,192] strand '-'. Reverse complement of M12927.1: v4.0.0 polyA-signal [7447,7453] only; 4.1.0 PPT [482,493] and polyA-signal [325,331], strand '-'. 200 random-interior LTR pairs (300-bp random LTR, 3 kb random interior, seeds 0-199): records with any PBS/PPT/PAS row 38/200 (PBS 12, PPT 6, PAS 23) in v4.0.0 versus 14/200 in 4.1.0 (PBS 2, PPT 7, PAS 8); cis_orientation 'undetermined' 186, '+' 9, '-' 5. Domain-strand path (engine.analyze): copia M11240.1 with the PPT and poly(A)-signal segments shuffled gave cis_orientation '+', source 'domain-strand' in 4.1.0; the PPT row was still reported there because the shuffled tract is still purine-rich.
limitations: A chance poly(A)-signal with a downstream element on the opposite strand can set the orientation wrongly and block the domain strand: copia with 50-70 bp around the PPT and signal replaced by random C/T or C/A sequence read cis_orientation '-' (source 'cis-elements') with a '-' strand AATAAA row, although the element is forward; the domain strand was not consulted because the cis rows had already decided.
The cis_orientation of '+' on bare, correctly oriented specimens rests on the PPT rather than the PBS; the PBS panel (tRNA-Lys3 only) is not an orientation witness unless confident.
Elements without domain hits and without cis evidence keep 'undetermined' and no PBS/PPT/PAS rows, where v4.0.0 would have reported forward-strand rows (often chance rows).
PBS rows on '-' elements are matched on the reverse complement; motifs are reported as read on the element's strand.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: take M11240.1 and reverse-complement it. v4.0.0: LTR + polyA-signal only (antisense), no PPT; 4.1.0: LTR + PPT [276,285] strand '-' + polyA-signal [186,192] strand '-', LTR row cis_orientation '-'. Negative: forward M11240.1 gives the same PPT and signal coordinates in both versions; random-interior LTR pairs (200 seeds) give cis rows in about 19% (v4.0.0) versus 7% (4.1.0). Boundary: an LTR element whose PPT and signal are destroyed but with an RT/INT hit: 'undetermined' first, then 'domain-strand' source and restored rows in 4.1.0; if a chance AATAAA+DSE exists on the wrong strand the orientation is set wrongly by cis-elements (documented limitation).
records.changelog_line: LTR cis-elements (PBS, PPT, poly(A) signal) are reported on the element's own strand, using the domain strand when the structure alone cannot orient the element.

records.title: Amplicon sequence carries the primer's own bases over its whole footprint
records.before: amplicon.seq = (5' tail of the left oligo) + template[left:right] + reverse complement of the right oligo's tail, so bases inside the annealed core came from the template even where the primer mismatches, and a tailed primer with default max_mm 2 could start with template bases rather than its own sequence.
records.after: seq = left oligo + template between the two annealed footprints + reverse complement of the right oligo (overlapping footprints: the left oligo covers the overlap and the leading characters of the reverse-complemented right oligo are dropped), so len(seq) == product_length and the product begins with the forward oligo and ends with the reverse complement of the reverse oligo. Coordinates, mismatch counts, tail and anneal lengths are unchanged. Degenerate primers now put IUPAC letters into seq.

records.measured: Run in this audit on M11240 (F = GGATCC + bases 1000-1020, R = GAATTC + reverse complement of 1300-1320): coordinates, anneal lengths and mismatches are identical in both versions (994-1322, 332 bp, anneal 26/22, tails 0/4, mismatches 2/2; the permitted mismatches let the core extend into the 6-nt tail), but seq starts with the forward oligo and ends with the reverse-complemented reverse oligo only in 4.1.0 (4.0.0: false/false); len(seq) equals product_length in both. records.title: Primer table gains Location and Notes columns and is reordered; exports gain the matching columns
records.before: PRIMER_COLS began with the pair id and sequences; there was no location or caution text, and Struct/Penalty were later columns.
records.after: PRIMER_COLS order: ID, Struct, Penalty, Location, Notes, Forward, Reverse, Product, Fwd pos, Rev pos, Tm F/R, GC% F/R, Hairpin, Self-dim, Hetero, 3'-end. Location = product span, then the segment each primer overlaps (5' flank, 5' LTR/TIR, internal, 3' repeat, 3' flank) from the accepted terminal-repeat pair of widest extent, plus '(DOMAIN)' when a primer lies wholly inside a domain hit; a pair designed on another template reads 'a-b on <label>'. Notes flags (a) a primer whose 3' 18-nt core lies inside one terminal-repeat copy ('may also bind the other copy and solo copies'; for a TIR 'may prime from the inverted ... arm'), (b) pairs whose forward and reverse sites both overlap ('≈P2'), (c) a primer shared by two pairs ('same F as ...'). It flags; it never removes a pair. Exports carry 'Location (0-based, half-open)' and Notes.

records.title: PBS rows report a composition-adjusted chance probability; PBS panel scope stated on LTR rows
records.before: v4.0.0: a PBS row carried identity, confidence and a note that a weak match is 'endogenised PBS is often diverged'; no estimate of how often a leader window matches by chance and no statement that the panel is tRNA-Lys3 only. About 14% of random 300-nt leaders returned a row at the unchanged 55% floor.
records.after: 4.1.0: every PBS row carries chance_probability (Poisson-binomial over the 18 positions from the record's composition, over all leader windows tested), the panel list, and, when the match is sub-confident, a note quoting the chance ('a match this good arises by chance in about N% of leaders of this composition'). The accepted LTR row carries pbs_scope: 'PBS search covers tRNA-Lys3 only; an element primed by another tRNA (e.g. initiator tRNA-Met in Ty1/copia) is not assessed, so no PBS row is not no PBS'. Match counting uses A/C/G/T only. Reporting floor (0.55), confident threshold (0.72), search window (44 nt) and the panel are unchanged.
records.trigger: Every PBS row and every LTR row.

records.before: v4.0.0: no function reported what the terminal-repeat scans can see; the 1200-bp TIR window was an inline literal; a long record with no LTR or TIR gave no note and classification said 'no terminal repeat was accepted' without qualification.
records.after: 4.1.0: scan_scope(seq) returns record_bp, ltr_seed_window_bp (min(n//2, 6000)), tir_seed_window_bp (min(n//2, 1200)), tir_joint_window_bp (min(n//2, 400)), tail_window_bp (min(n, 600)) and covers_whole_record. After structural detection (and any orientation re-run), when no LTR or TIR row exists and 2 x a seed window is below the record length, engine.analyze appends a record note quoting the record length, the LTR and/or TIR seed windows, the 600-bp tail window and, when 2 x the TIR window is below the length, a sentence that more than 1200 bp of flank on a side hides the element's ends from the TIR scan. classify appends the same windows to its 'no terminal repeat' sentences for records longer than the windows.

records.title: Low-complexity seed masking and occurrence caps for LTR and TIR seed search (speed)
records.before: v4.0.0: _kmer_index kept every seed word, so a low-complexity or repeat-rich window produced seed pairs quadratically (a homopolymer window gave millions of pairs): A5000 3.0 s, (AT)n 3 kb 0.67 s, (GATC)n 3 kb 0.54 s, 5%-diverged (AT)n 0.46 s in find_ltr + find_tir + detect_all on the reference machine.
records.after: 4.1.0: seed words seen more than 20 times in one search window are dropped (both LTR windows and both TIR windows, query and index side). LTR seeds are additionally masked where a DUST score (64-bp window, triplet score above 2.0, dustmasker's default level 20) flags the sequence, and a word masked in either window seeds nothing. TIR 11-mer/6-mer seeds use the occurrence cap only (DUST would mask 9-20% of the Ac and Tc1 specimens and change real calls). At most 64 densest diagonals are kept per TIR seed search; the per-diagonal seed density uses a bisect over sorted anchors instead of a quadratic sum. Seed-pair loop order is preserved so diagonal ties break as before.
records.trigger: Low-complexity or repeat-rich records (microsatellites, homopolymers, tandem arrays) and flank windows; no effect on non-repetitive sequence.
affected_outputs: wall time of the structural stage
no change to row values on ordinary sequence (905-record corpus identical in the wave record)
LTR/TIR seeds on low-complexity windows are absent, so candidates that existed only through masked seeds are no longer produced

parameters.basis: new; Morgulis et al. 2006, dustmasker default window

records.measured: Own run, detect_all in-process, seconds v4.0.0 -> 4.1.0: (AT)1500 0.67 -> 0.005; A5000 3.03 -> 0.004; (CAG)700 0.22 -> 0.003; (GATC)750 0.54 -> 0.004; 5%-diverged (AT)1500 0.46 -> 0.025; random 6 kb 0.003 -> 0.006; bare specimens 0.001-0.002 -> 0.002-0.006. The 44.6 s (find_tir on (AT)3000) and 99 s figures in the wave records belong to an intermediate pre-release state of the code and are not v4.0.0 timings. Wave record: 905-record corpus (5 bare specimens, 5 specimens x 60 seeds x with/without planted TSD, 300 random records) identical before and after masking; DUST masks 1.5-1.8% of copia and gypsy seed words.
limitations: A record whose terminal repeat is itself low-complexity (a microsatellite-rich LTR) loses its LTR seeds under DUST; no such real case was tested.
Diverged tandem arrays still pass through a gapped band alignment bounded only by the 250,000-cell cap: worst case 1.54 s in a stress sweep of 144 arrays (20-bp unit, 20% divergence, 9 kb).
find_tir on a 5%- or 20%-diverged (AT)n takes 41-60 ms because the TIR search uses the occurrence cap only.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive (speed): time detect_all on A5000, (AT)1500 and a 5%-diverged (AT)1500: v4.0.0 3.0, 0.67 and 0.46 s; 4.1.0 below 0.03 s (single process, one core). Negative: bare M11240.1, M12927.1, X01005.1, X05424.1 and M80343.1 must give identical structural rows in both versions. Boundary: any benchmark corpus with a hard timeout should show no 4.1.0 timeout; results for ordinary sequence must be identical row-for-row.
records.changelog_line: Terminal-repeat detection no longer stalls on microsatellite- or AT-rich records: low-complexity and over-represented seed words are masked (a DUST score for LTR seeds, an occurrence cap for LTR and TIR seeds), so such records scan in milliseconds instead of tens of seconds, ...

records.title: ERV evidence sentence names 'errantivirus' only for Gypsy-called elements; Copia/Gypsy evidence wording
records.before: Any record with an RT, accepted LTRs and an ENV hit got 'envelope (env) domain present with paired LTRs → endogenous retrovirus (ERV) / errantivirus lineage (an env-bearing LTR retroelement)'. The Copia/Gypsy evidence sentences read 'integrase N-terminal to RT + paired LTRs → Copia/Ty1 order' and 'integrase C-terminal to RT + paired LTRs → Gypsy/Ty3 order'.
records.after: The ERV sentence reads 'env-bearing LTR retroelement (ERV architecture)' and appends '; errantivirus lineage for a Gypsy element' only when the superfamily starts with Gypsy. The Copia/Gypsy sentences read 'integrase N-terminal to RT (INT before RT, the Copia/Ty1-type domain order) + paired LTRs → Copia superfamily' and the Gypsy equivalent, so a superfamily is no longer presented as a Wicker order. The is_erv flag and its rule (RT and LTR and ENV, and not a co-oriented DIRS call) are unchanged.
records.trigger: Every record with is_erv True (sentence) and every Copia or Gypsy call (sentences).
labels_renamed: evidence text 'ERV / errantivirus lineage' -> 'ERV architecture' (+ errantivirus clause only for Gypsy)
evidence text 'Copia/Ty1 order' -> 'Copia superfamily' (and Gypsy/Ty3 equivalent)
records.measured: Hand-built Gypsy layout with a TLV_coat ENV hit (te_class and confidence unchanged, LTR/Gypsy High): old text 'endogenous retrovirus (ERV) / errantivirus lineage', new text 'env-bearing LTR retroelement (ERV architecture; errantivirus lineage for a Gypsy element)'. For AY037928 the new text ends 'ERV architecture)' without errantivirus.
limitations: Wording only; any text-matching benchmark harness keyed on the old sentences will not find them.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: AY037928 (old evidence contains 'errantivirus', 4.1.0 does not). Control: a Drosophila gypsy-type layout with an env hit stays 'errantivirus lineage for a Gypsy element'. Boundary: AJ289709 (HERV-H, TLV_coat) is Gypsy-called so still carries the errantivirus clause.
records.changelog_line: Covered by the first [4.1.0] Changed bullet only for the errantivirus clause ('"Errantivirus" is named only for Gypsy-called elements'); the Copia/Gypsy evidence rewording is missing from CHANGELOG.

records.title: 'Insertion site captured / both termini present' wording requires a non-chance-level TSD
records.before: In the DNA-transposon branch, a TSD flanking an accepted TIR pair was reported as 'the insertion site itself is captured, so both element termini are present in the record' whenever its length was congruent or the superfamily had no expected length.
records.after: That sentence is emitted only when the TSD row has chance_level False. A chance-level row, or a row with no chance estimate, gets 'a target-site duplication flanks the inverted repeats (<congruence note>), but a flanking direct repeat of N bp is short enough to arise by chance (p = ...) [or: its chance probability was not assessed], so it is not credited as the insertion site and does not confirm the element ends'. The incongruent wording is unchanged apart from range/motif quoting (CLS-017). The LTR branch never claimed a captured site and has no chance clause.
records.trigger: DNA-transposon calls (hAT, Tc1/Mariner, CACTA, MULE, IS4-like, DDE) with an accepted TIR and a TSD row; a 2 bp TSD is always chance level.
affected_outputs: evidence/evidenceLedger sentence about the insertion site
labels_renamed: evidence 'insertion site itself is captured ... both element termini are present' -> chance-hedged sentence (for chance-level or unassessed TSD rows)

parameters.name: CHANCE_LEVEL_P (TSD chance-level flag threshold)
parameters.v4_0_0: absent (no chance fields on TSD rows)
parameters.basis: a single pre-specified 5 bp match is about 1e-3 under uniform composition; adjusted for lengths and boundary placements searched

records.measured: Hand-built rows: hAT 8 bp chance_level False 'captured' in both; hAT 8 bp chance_level True: 'captured' (4.0.0) -> chance clause (4.1.0); CACTA 3 bp and Tc1/Mariner 2 bp (always chance level): 'captured' -> chance clause; rows without chance_level: 'captured' -> 'chance probability was not assessed'. End-to-end flanked records (30 per cell): X05424 with a random 8 bp TSD: 'captured' sentence 27/30 in 4.1.0 and 0/30 in 4.0.0 (4.0.0 found no TSD row at all, see CLS-035); X01005 with TA: 0/30 captured in 4.1.0 (hedged sentence 30/30).
limitations: Evidence text only; confidence and completeness tier do not depend on the TSD.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: flanked X05424 with an 8 bp TSD: 4.1.0 emits the 'captured' sentence, 4.0.0 emits none. Negative: flanked X01005 with TA (hedged in 4.1.0). Boundary: hAT with a 7 bp or 9 bp TSD (not congruent).
records.changelog_line: TSD congruence uses superfamily length ranges (LTR 4–6 bp, preferred 5 bp) and motifs (Tc1/Mariner TA), and a short chance-level repeat is no longer described as proof that the insertion site is captured.

records.title: Standalone-TIR evidence quotes the 22,500-sequence ceiling and adds a composition caution
records.before: The evidence for a TIR >= 20 bp with no transposase said 'Chance inverted repeats reached at most 17 bp over 4,500 random sequences' (the 17 bp figure was measured over five seeds and 22,500 sequences; 15 bp at the recorded single seed). No composition qualification.
records.after: The sentence quotes CHANCE_TIR_MAX_BP (17) 'across 22,500 random sequences (five seeds, checked at 35-65% GC)'. For a record outside 35-65% GC, or where the record's own composition makes an exact repeat of that length likely (probability > 1e-3), a caution is appended giving the GC and the composition-specific chance probability and asking for a flanking TSD or a transposase before relying on the call. The call, confidence and class are unchanged.
records.trigger: DNA/non-autonomous calls from a TIR of >= 20 bp with no transposase (and the host-like-domain variant, CLS-012); caution only for GC below 35% or above 65%, or high per-record chance probability.
labels_renamed: evidence '17 bp over 4,500 random sequences' -> '17 bp across 22,500 random sequences (five seeds, checked at 35-65% GC)'

parameters.name: CHANCE_TIR_MAX_BP
parameters.basis: longest chance inverted repeat over five seeds

parameters.name: CHANCE_TIR_SEQUENCES
parameters.basis: sequences behind the five-seed maximum; the 4.0.0 text quoted the single-seed count with the five-seed length

parameters.name: CHANCE_TIR_GC_RANGE
parameters.basis: GC range over which the ceiling was checked (50% GC benchmark, seeded tests at 35% and 65%)

parameters.name: MIN_TIR_STANDALONE
parameters.basis: unchanged floor

records.measured: Hand-built 31 bp TIR with seq at GC 50%: sentence changes only. At GC 31%, 21% and 80%: extra caution with composition-specific p of 6.8e-12, 1.1e-09 and 2.1e-09 respectively. 25 bp TIR + Chromo at 21% GC: caution present. End-to-end synthetic 31 bp arms in a 24% GC random 1.5 kb record: same class (DNA/non-autonomous, Candidate) in both versions; caution only in 4.1.0.
limitations: Caution is text only; it does not change the class or confidence, so an AT-rich chance inverted repeat of >= 20 bp is still called DNA/non-autonomous.
Chance probability is exact-arm; an imperfect arm is likelier by chance.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: a synthetic 31 bp inverted pair in a 25% GC record: identical call in both, caution only in 4.1.0 evidence. Negative: same pair at 50% GC (no caution). Boundary: 34% GC versus 36% GC.
records.changelog_line: A live, seeded chance-TIR check runs with the test suite and guards the 20-bp standalone-TIR rule. (The evidence wording and the composition caution are missing from CHANGELOG.)

records.title: Scan-scope statements when no terminal repeat is found in a record longer than the scan windows
records.before: 'no terminal inverted-repeat pair recovered' and 'no terminal repeat was accepted' were unqualified, and no note said how far from each end the scans looked.
records.after: classify appends '(the record is N bp and terminal repeats were searched only within W bp of each end)' (TIR: 'short or imperfect terminal repeats were searched only within 400 bp' when the 1,200 bp seed window already covers the record) to the TIR-absent sentence and the two LTR-absent sentences (RT+chromodomain; RT+DDE integrase). engine.analyze adds a record note naming the LTR/TIR seed windows and the 600 bp tail window when no LTR/TIR row was found and the windows do not cover the record.
records.trigger: Records of roughly 800 bp or longer (TIR), 12,000 bp or longer (LTR windows of 6,000 bp each side), or any odd-length record with no terminal repeat found.

parameters.name: terminal-repeat scan windows (LTR seed, TIR seed, TIR joint, tail)
parameters.basis: windows unchanged; now stated

records.measured: Hand-built: hAT with no TIR on a 5,000 bp record gets the parenthetical in 4.1.0 only; RT+INT on a 30,000 bp record gets 'searched only within 6,000 bp of each end'. Engine notes: M80343 (6,050 bp) gains the scope note. Boundary defect found: any odd-length record gets the statement even when the windows cover all but one base (n=701, 375, 2001, 5000 all emit it; n=700 does not) because the windows are n//2.
limitations: Odd-length records get a scope statement that overstates the unsearched region (1 bp in the middle) because 2*(n//2) < n.
Wording only.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: a 5,000 bp record with no TIR (4.1.0 adds the parenthetical). Negative: a 700 bp record (none). Boundary: 700 bp versus 701 bp records (the odd-length defect).
records.changelog_line: missing from CHANGELOG

records.title: Helitron evidence no longer claims TIR absence when a TIR was detected
records.before: The Helitron evidence always ended 'the absence of TIR/TSD here is expected and is not evidence against a Helitron', even when a TIR row existed.
records.after: When a credited TIR exists the sentence reads '; a terminal inverted repeat was detected in this record, which is not a Helitron feature (it may belong to another element or be coincidental)'. The Helitron call itself (domain-only; 'Helitron-family helicase present — superfamily not called', te_class unclassified) is unchanged.
records.trigger: HEL (PF14214) hit together with an accepted TIR row.
records.measured: Hand-built 25 bp TIR + Helitron_like_N: text changes; te_class, superfamily, confidence and outcome unchanged; completeness kind 'DNA transposon' -> 'terminal inverted repeat (class unassigned)' (CLS-013).
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: any record with a Helitron helicase hit and a >=10 bp TIR (text change only). Negative: Helitron without TIR (unchanged). Boundary: none.
records.changelog_line: missing from CHANGELOG

records.title: Coding-axis note counts ORFs and recognises the canonical LINE ORF1/ORF2 layout
records.before: completeness.coding.note read 'the detected domains fall in N separate reading frame(s) ... consistent with an interrupted, rearranged or degenerate copy' where N counted host ORFs (a sequence has six frames, so 8 was possible); an intact LINE (M80343) was described as a possibly degenerate copy.
records.after: The note reads 'N separate ORFs (frames +2, ...)' listing frames, and for two ORFs on one strand where ORF1p precedes an endonuclease-RT ORF it says 'consistent with the canonical LINE ORF1/ORF2 organisation (ORF1p, then the endonuclease–RT ORF)'. The completeness.coding.state string is unchanged.
records.trigger: Records whose detected domains fall in two or more ORFs.
records.measured: M80343: v4.0.0 '2 separate reading frame(s) — consistent with an interrupted, rearranged or degenerate copy ...'; 4.1.0 '2 separate ORFs (frames +2) — consistent with the canonical LINE ORF1/ORF2 organisation'. Hand-built 8 RT hits in 8 ORFs: '8 separate reading frame(s)' -> '8 separate ORFs (frames +0, +1, +2)'.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: M80343 (text change). Negative: M11240 (single-ORF coding, unchanged state). Boundary: ORF1 downstream of the RT ORF (not the canonical layout, old wording kept).
records.changelog_line: missing from CHANGELOG

records.title: Truncation note only for an open-ended ORF that carries a detected domain, naming the end
records.before: Any open-ended ORF (a 40-aa ATG..end stretch in any frame) produced 'sequence appears 3′-truncated — some ORFs are open-ended; domain calls on them may be partial', so intact reference elements (X01005, X05424, M80343) carried it.
records.after: A note is added only when an ORF that hosts at least one detected domain is open-ended, naming the end (forward ORF open at the 3′ end, reverse-strand ORF open at the 5′ end): 'an ORF carrying a detected domain runs off the 3′ [and/or 5′] end(s) of the supplied sequence — the element may be truncated there ...'.
records.trigger: Records with open-ended ORFs; the note now requires a domain-hosting one.
labels_renamed: note 'sequence appears 3′-truncated — some ORFs are open-ended ...' -> 'an ORF carrying a detected domain runs off the 3′/5′ end ...'
records.measured: v4.0.0 vs 4.1.0: X01005 (full), X05424, M80343, X05424 flanked and several synthetic records carried the old note in 4.0.0 and none in 4.1.0. M11240[:3500] (cut copia): old generic note; 4.1.0 names the 3′ end; its reverse complement names the 5′ end. X01005[:800]: names the 3′ end. M11240 last 3500 bp: no note either version. Classification is identical in all of these.
limitations: A cut that removes the start codon region of an ORF (5′-truncation of a forward ORF) is not signalled.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: M11240[:3500] (3′ note names the end) and X01005[:800]. Negative: complete X01005 or M12927 (no note in 4.1.0, generic note in 4.0.0). Boundary: reverse complement of the cut record (5′ end).
records.changelog_line: The truncation note appears only when an ORF carrying a detected domain runs off a sequence end and names that end, so intact reference elements no longer read as truncated.

records.title: Family panel partitions RepeatMasker hits into TE, tandem/low-complexity, unclassified and other (RNA gene) and keys its blank-result caveats on the defaulted lineage
records.before: Hits were split into TE / non-TE / unclassified by two hand-kept class sets (_NONTE, _UNCLASSED); RNA genes and artefacts fell into the TE list; the 'no organism set' caveat was triggered when the species string did not start with '(all'.
records.after: _partition_hits uses the backend classifier wsl.repeat_kind so the panel and the whole-genome landscape agree: TE, tandem (low-complexity and satellites), unclassified ('Unknown') and other (RNA genes, artefacts, listed apart and not counted as TE family calls); the panel header names the strongest TE class; the blank-result caveats key on species_defaulted / lineage_searched, so RepeatMasker's default lineage is no longer read as an organism choice; the family and splice controls are disarmed and the library choice cleared when the backend is lost.
records.trigger: Every family annotation result display.
affected_outputs: table grouping and notes in panel 03; the data returned by wsl.annotate is unchanged
records.measured: From code (the 4.0.0 and 4.1.0 renderers compared); hit data unchanged (GEN-006 measurement).
limitations: Classification of a hit as TE depends on the class string Dfam supplies.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: annotate a locus with an snRNA hit: 4.0.0 lists it with the TE hits, 4.1.0 lists it under other annotations. Negative: a Copia hit lists as TE in both. Boundary: 'Unknown' class stays unclassified.

records.measured: From tests and the wave record (live esummary).
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: fetch M11240: status shows replaced, replacedBy X04456 in 4.1.0 only. Negative: X04456 status live. Boundary: n/a.
