records.title: Whole-genome annotation sizes disk from the source FASTA, checks space before the download, numbers resumed progress and marks completion
records.before: Disk need was int(search-target bytes / GiB) + 2 although the 2bit target is about a quarter of the FASTA that annotation must re-fetch; the FASTA download started without a free-space check; a resumed run restarted at 1 of N; a completed run re-run with other settings was refused as 'part-finished'.
records.after: genome_prepare records fasta_bytes (genome_list returns it); annotate_budget(genome_bytes, fasta_bytes, fasta_cached) uses ceil(k x FASTA / GiB) + 2 with k = 2 (FASTA must be re-downloaded) or 1 (cached; the panel sends no fasta_cached, so it stays conservative); the script checks 2 x FASTA + 1 GiB free (smaller of WSL and Windows backing volume) before downloading (4 x the 2bit size for caches without fasta_bytes); progress starts at the chunks already done; a .complete marker makes a settings clash read 'a completed annotation ... exists with different settings' and genome_annotate returns annotation_state complete or part_finished; the cost dialog shows the error and a 'Check again' button when the budget probe fails.
records.trigger: Whole-genome annotation of large genomes; resumed runs.

parameters.name: disk_needed_gb basis
parameters.v4_1_0: ceil(k x FASTA bytes / GiB) + 2, k = 2 (not cached) or 1 (cached)
parameters.basis: the zip and the extracted FASTA coexist during extraction

parameters.name: pre-download free-space floor
parameters.basis: download plus extraction plus margin

records.measured: Run in this audit through engine.run_annotate_budget on this machine: genome_bytes 800 MB with fasta_bytes 3.1 GB sent: 4.0.0 ignores fasta_bytes and returns disk_needed_gb 2 (from the search target only); 4.1.0 returns 8 (k = 2) and, with fasta_cached true, 5 (k = 1); genome_bytes alone returns 2 in both versions. No whole-genome annotation was run.
limitations: Genomes prepared before 4.1.0 lack fasta_bytes and use the 4x fallback estimate.
The annotation directory is not keyed by run signature, so a completed run must be discarded to re-run with new settings.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: engine.run_annotate_budget({genome_bytes: 800e6, fasta_bytes: 3.1e9}): disk_needed_gb 8 in 4.1.0 versus 2 in 4.0.0. Negative: genome_bytes only: 2 in both. Boundary: fasta_cached true gives 5 (k = 1).
records.changelog_line: Manage genomes, the annotation cost dialog and whole-genome annotation progress recover correctly after failures; deleting a genome warns that its annotation is deleted with it. (The FASTA-based disk sizing and pre-download check are missing from CHANGELOG.)

records.title: The backend skips container-runtime distributions and distributions without bash or python3, and remembers its distro
records.before: resolve_distro returned the Windows default distro or the first listed, so Docker Desktop's distro could become the backend; envcheck reported 'available' for any listing containing 'Running' or 'Stopped'.
records.after: The distro table is parsed once; docker-desktop(-data), rancher-desktop(-data) and podman-machine-default are never candidates; candidates are tried as remembered distro (wsl_distro.txt), Windows default, then the rest, and one is chosen only if it has bash and python3 (a timeout counts as unknown); set_distro pins a choice; envcheck.probe_backends reports 'available' only when a non-runtime distro exists, else 'no distro'.
records.trigger: Machines with Docker/Rancher/Podman distros, several distros, or a default distro without bash.
affected_outputs: which distro all annotation, genome and splice jobs run in

parameters.name: runtime-distro skip list
parameters.basis: these distros have no usable bash/conda

parameters.name: distro usability probe timeout (s)
parameters.basis: cold start allowance

records.measured: Live (this audit): on this machine (Ubuntu-24.04 only) both versions resolve 'Ubuntu-24.04'; the Docker case is covered by unit tests only.
limitations: The remembered distro outranks the Windows default, so changing the default later does not move the backend unless set_distro is called.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: a machine with docker-desktop as the Windows default and Ubuntu installed: 4.0.0 selects docker-desktop and fails, 4.1.0 selects Ubuntu. Negative: Ubuntu only: identical. Boundary: a default distro that lacks python3 is skipped.
records.changelog_line: The backend skips Docker Desktop and other unsuitable distributions.

records.title: WSL failures are diagnosed (still starting, no bash, start failed, restart pending) and unregister is advised only after a confirmed start failure
records.before: Any failed WSL probe read 'registered but won't start' with 'wsl --unregister' advice; restart-pending existed only as dialog memory; a Windows install log with no terminal marker counted as running forever; a failed first status probe left an empty window.
records.after: available() returns reason timeout | starting | no_bash | start_failed (only on a WSL error code) | unknown | no_suitable_distro; components_status gives per-reason guidance and offers wsl --unregister only for start_failed, with a warning that it deletes the home directory, Dfam libraries and cached genomes. The Windows install log state is none | running | stale (no marker and older than 2 h or than the last boot) | done | failed; components_status returns installing False plus wsl2_installing, wsl2_install_stale and reboot_pending; a reopened dialog attaches to a running Windows install, releases it when stale, and retries a failed first probe up to 3 times before asking for Refresh.
records.trigger: Cold WSL starts, restarts, installs interrupted by reboot.
labels_renamed: installing (folded Windows install flag) -> separate wsl2_installing

parameters.name: stale Windows install log (s)
parameters.basis: an install that writes no marker for 2 h is abandoned

parameters.name: automatic status-probe retries
parameters.basis: UI robustness

records.measured: Unit tests with stubbed probes; not exercised on a WSL-less machine.
limitations: Not verified on a machine without WSL; the elevated install path is unchanged apart from GEN-018.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: wsl.components_status with available() returning reason timeout: 4.1.0 says 'still starting', 4.0.0 advises unregister. Negative: healthy WSL: identical. Boundary: a log older than the last boot with DONE-WSL is no longer a pending restart.
records.changelog_line: The backend diagnoses why WSL did not answer before suggesting wsl --unregister.

records.title: 'Install / update all' continues past a failing component and skips only its dependents
records.before: The install script ran the steps in one shell, so a failing step (for example minimap2) ended the script and the independent Dfam steps never ran.
records.after: Each step is a function run in its own subshell (a failure ends only that step); a step whose prerequisite failed or was skipped is skipped (_STEP_NEEDS: repeatmasker, minimap2, miniprot, genomescan, viennarna need micromamba; famdb_conf needs repeatmasker); the run ends with one SUMMARY line and a single terminal '[teagle] FAILED: not installed: ...' (or DONE). Mid-run '[teagle] STEP x FAILED' lines are not terminal markers.
records.trigger: Any backend install with one failing component.
affected_outputs: components installed after a partial failure
records.measured: Real bash run with a failing minimap2 step in the wave record: Dfam steps ran after it.
limitations: A failing step leaves a partial environment that the next install call repairs.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: force the minimap2 step to fail: 4.0.0 never installs Dfam, 4.1.0 installs it and reports the failure. Negative: all steps succeed: DONE in both. Boundary: micromamba fails: every dependent is skipped.
records.changelog_line: missing from CHANGELOG

records.title: The shared 'te' conda environment is adopted and removed only when TEagle created it; a different micromamba is backed up
records.before: An existing environment named 'te' was adopted and reinstalled into whoever created it; a different ~/bin/micromamba was overwritten without a copy; clean install removed envs/te unconditionally.
records.after: 'te' is adopted only with ~/micromamba/envs/te/.teagle-owned or the pinned RepeatMasker from an earlier TEagle install (then marked); new environments are marked at creation; any other 'te' is left untouched and the step fails with a message. A different ~/bin/micromamba is copied to micromamba.pre-teagle first. records.title: NCBI/ENA requests retry rate limits and server errors, are paced, and report failures in plain language; feature fetch failures are not cached
records.before: _get made one attempt (User-Agent 'TEagle/0.1'), turned HTTP 429/5xx into a bare 'HTTP n from source', cached a transient feature-table failure permanently, and rewrote source.retrievedUtc on a coordinate cache hit.

records.title: chance_tir() and the live seeded chance-TIR guard for the 20-bp standalone floor
records.before: v4.0.0: MIN_TIR_STANDALONE (20 bp) was justified by a recorded benchmark file (22,500 random sequences, ceiling 17 bp) read by no live test; classification quoted the ceiling with no composition dependence.
records.after: 4.1.0: structural.chance_tir(seq, length) returns the chance, from the record's own base composition, that random sequence holds a perfect inverted repeat of that length between the two outer seed windows (p = 1 - exp(-W^2 q^length), q = 2(fA fT + fC fG)), with gc, placements, per_placement, chance_probability and in_measured_gc_range (35-65% GC). It is used by classify for a composition-aware chance caution. A live seeded measurement of find_tir on random sequence (seed 41, 450 sequences, and 1,800 sequences) runs in the test suite and fails if the longest chance TIR approaches the 20-bp floor. MIN_TIR_STANDALONE is unchanged.
records.trigger: Every TIR classification (the caution text); test suite.
affected_outputs: classification evidence wording for TIR (chance probability and GC range)
labels_added: chance_tir() return keys gc, placements, per_placement, chance_probability, in_measured_gc_range

parameters.name: MIN_TIR_STANDALONE
parameters.basis: frozen; the length at or above which a TIR licenses a Class II call with no transposase

parameters.name: CHANCE_TIR_GC_RANGE
parameters.basis: new; GC range over which the ceiling was checked

parameters.name: CHANCE_TIR_MAX_BP / CHANCE_TIR_SEQUENCES (classify)
parameters.basis: values unchanged; now sealed

records.measured: Own run: chance_tir on a random 3-kb record at length 17: gc 0.513, per_placement 5.9e-11, chance_probability 8.5e-05. Wave records: longest chance TIR 17 bp over 1,800 sequences (44 hits), 16 bp over 450 at seed 41, 16 bp at 20%/65% GC; five-seed ceiling re-measured after the flanked search 15, 17, 16, 17, 15 bp. Own random-record run (200 records per GC, seeds 1000-1199): longest TIR row 17 bp (50% GC) and 14 bp (35% GC) in both versions.
limitations: The model is exact-arm only and understates imperfect arms; the live detector bound holds for arms of 14 bp and longer.
The ceiling holds for 1.5-9 kb random templates in the 35-65% GC range; chance repeat length grows with template length.
records.benchmark_probe: Positive: run find_tir on 450 random sequences (seed 41, 1.5, 4 and 9 kb): the longest reported TIR must stay below 20 bp in both versions (16-17 bp observed). Negative: a 20-bp perfect inverted repeat planted in random sequence is called in both. Boundary: 17-18 bp planted perfect arms in 4.1.0 flanked records are reported with boundary_uncertain and, being below 20 bp, do not license a Class II call.
records.changelog_line: A live, seeded chance-TIR check runs with the test suite and guards the 20-bp standalone-TIR rule.

Results freeze: reporting/REPORT_LOCK.json (12 source tables), RESULTS_FREEZE.json, ARCHIVE_MANIFEST, PACKAGE_ALLOWLIST, validators/validate_primary.py and validate_independent.py, deterministic rebuild; 152-member archive. Analysis families are never pooled: ORIGINAL_1_0_0, AMENDED_A1, AMENDED_A2, AMENDED_I2_INTEGRATION, AMENDED_D1_STRESS, AMENDED_P2_SYNTHETIC_SPECIFICITY, AMENDED_R1_DEPLOYMENT, AMENDED_FUNCTION_COMPLETION (deviations DEV-01..DEV-18). TEagle fields read below are therefore taken from the protocol contracts (parameter_locks.json teagle_output_rules, a1_crosswalk_lock + apply_a1_crosswalk.py, r1_lock, i2 bundle schema, P2 templates) and are labelled 'protocol contract, adapter not inspected' where applicable. endpoints.question: Selective classification: how often does TEagle (vs TEsorter 1.5.1, RepeatClassifier 2.0.9, PASTEClassifier 2.0) commit to class/order/superfamily labels that agree with curated-library header labels, and how often does it withhold, fail or fall outside the label space? Descriptive, post-raw/pre-score crosswalk, no superiority claim.
endpoints.inputs: 180 nucleotide sequences from frozen EDTA 2.2.2 curated libraries (rice 7.0.0, maize MTEC 2019-11-12, Arabidopsis) plus 30 biological non-TE controls from UniProtKB 2026_02/RefSeq CDS frames (10 per organism). Strata (30 each): ltr_retrotransposon, non_ltr_retrotransposon, tir_dna_transposon, rolling_circle, non_autonomous_or_incomplete, biological_non_te. Eligibility: IUPAC DNA, 80-50,000 bp, no exact normalized match to Dfam 3.6 / Dfam 4.0 nucleotide resources or development fixtures. Selection key SHA-256 of '410101:<source_id>:<header>:<seq_sha256>' (non-TE '410103:<taxon>:<acc.version>:<seq_sha256>'). Truth = library header mapped by truth_rules (label is curated-library agreement, not adjudicated truth).
endpoints.n_units: 180 records x 4 methods x 3 ranks = 2160 rank rows (TEagle 540). Sources: arabidopsis_edta_2_2_2 55, maize_mtec_2019_11_12 40, rice_edta_7_0_0 85. Reported TEagle 4.0.0 overall: class and order each 135 answered (77 correct, 58 incorrect), 18 withheld, 26 unsupported, 1 unresolved, 0 failed; superfamily 130 truth-scored (50 unscored), 30 answered/30 correct, 16 withheld, 19 unsupported, 65 unresolved. All strata and sources tabled in reporting/classification_metrics.tsv (312 rows, DEV-12). All inputs in stratum NO_NEAR_TARGET_RESOURCE_SIMILARITY.
teagle_fields_read: Harness-level (protocol contract, adapter not inspected; shape taken from toy/a1_crosswalk_input.tsv and apply_a1_crosswalk.py): raw_execution_state in {completed, withheld, failed, not_run} derived from classification.outcome == 'withheld' (outcome overrides labels), process/parse failure, or not attempted
classification.te_class (stored as raw_class; the ONLY TEagle field the crosswalk maps: exact_te_class table + completed_unclassified_label 'unclassified')
classification.order (stored raw_order; domain-architecture string such as 'INT-RT', NOT read by the TEagle mapping)
classification.superfamily (stored raw_superfamily; NOT read by the TEagle mapping)
classification.class is not read
endpoints.label_space: Canonical class: class_i_retrotransposon, class_ii_dna_transposon, non_te, unresolved. Order: ltr_retrotransposon, non_ltr_retrotransposon, dirs, tir_dna_transposon, rolling_circle, non_te, unresolved. Superfamily: copia, gypsy, line, dirs, hat, tc1_mariner, cacta, mule, is4_like_dde, helitron, unresolved. Method states: answered, withheld, failed, unsupported (non-empty label with no canonical mapping), unresolved (explicit completed unresolved), not_run. Truth superfamily 'unresolved' is excluded from the superfamily denominator but stays visible.
endpoints.scoring_rule: Per rank: N = answered+withheld+failed+unsupported+unresolved+not_run; coverage = answered/N; answered-case accuracy = correct/answered; withholding, failure, unsupported rates; committed-error rate = incorrect/N; correct-call yield = correct/N; Wilson 95% intervals; correctness 'true' only if truth_scored, state answered and canonical label equals truth; no p-values, no pooling, no ranking. TEagle label->canonical map is the exact_te_class table in label_maps (LTR/Copia, LTR/Gypsy, LTR/unclassified, LINE, DIRS, DNA/hAT, DNA/Tc1-Mariner, DNA/CACTA, DNA/MULE, DNA/IS4-like, DNA/non-autonomous, none); every other TEagle te_class string (for example DNA/DDE, DNA/unclassified, LTR/partial, retro/partial, retro/unassigned, repeat/structural-only) is UNSUPPORTED at all ranks by construction.

endpoints.question: Within-record terminal direct-repeat (DTR) and terminal inverted-repeat (ITR) state retrieval and interval localization on controlled synthetic constructs with exact truth.
endpoints.inputs: 48 synthetic sequences built from A1 templates (12 LTR, 12 TIR, 12 non-LTR, 12 rolling-circle; templates >= 400 unambiguous bases; seed 410102): 6 LTR cases with two identical 120-bp direct terminal repeats, 6 with independently shuffled termini (<= 60% identity); 6 TIR cases with 60-bp left terminus and exact reverse complement at right, 6 negative; non-LTR and rolling-circle negative for both features. Truth = 0-based half-open intervals. Generator reads only A1 FASTA, selection ledger and public lock.
endpoints.n_units: 48 records x 2 feature types. Reported: direct_terminal_repeat truth_positive 6/truth_negative 42, TP 6, FP 0, sensitivity 1.0 (Wilson 0.610-1.0), exact interval matches 6, endpoint MAE 0 bp; inverted_terminal_repeat positive 6, TP 6, FP 0, exact interval matches 5, endpoint MAE 0.083 bp, length MAE 0.167, IoU mean 0.997. Cluster = source template.
teagle_fields_read: Protocol contract only, adapter not inspected: record-level state per feature type from machine-readable structural events (record.structural[] entries whose type starts 'LTR (terminal direct repeat)' for direct and 'TIR (terminal inverted repeat)' for inverted) and, for localization, their five_prime and three_prime [start,end) intervals; S1 common_task.state_contract (positive/negative/withheld/failed/unsupported/not_run). Inference: the 4.0.0 event keys are type, five_prime, three_prime, identity, ltr_len/tir_len, tsd_state.
endpoints.label_space: Per feature: positive, negative, withheld, failed, unsupported, not_run; candidate matching global one-to-one by positive overlap, maximizing matched pairs then overlap then minimizing endpoint error.
endpoints.scoring_rule: record_precision, sensitivity, false_positive_rate, correct_state_yield (Wilson), candidate_emitted/matched/extra, exact_interval_matches, endpoint_mae_bp_mean, length_mae_bp_mean, interval_iou_mean, overlap_f1_mean; synthetic only, no biological claim, never pooled with S1.

endpoints.question: Do workflow bundles detect eight injected defect classes (and accept pristine bundles), for TEagle vs three manual chains? Operational integrity only, not biological accuracy.
endpoints.inputs: 48 deterministic 6,000-bp synthetic base cases (root seed 410111; 8 archetypes x 6: complete_terminal_evidence, partial_terminal_evidence, conflicting_terminal_evidence, synthetic_non_te_control, unsupported_classification_rank, declared_module_failure, no_admissible_primer_pair, capped_specificity_search), pristine plus matched defect task = 96 tasks; defects: input_sequence_substitution_after_analysis, stale_classification_artifact, one_base_coordinate_shift, primer_table_swap_between_cases, collapsed_unresolved_state, removed_tool_or_database_identity, truncated_specificity_presented_complete, manifest_digest_mismatch.
endpoints.n_units: 48 base cases x 4 conditions (teagle, manual_chain_a/b/c) = 192 bundles; reported per condition 48/48 pristine accepted, 48/48 defects detected, 6 collapsed-unresolved and 6 removed-identity detected; 36 rows in reporting/integration_metrics.tsv.
teagle_fields_read: Schema i2-canonical-task-bundle-1 (protocol contract): input.sequence_sha256; operation_states{classification,domains,primers,specificity,structure}; artifacts.classification{artifact_sha256,case_id}, artifacts.domains.artifact_sha256, artifacts.primers{artifact_sha256,table_sha256}, artifacts.specificity{artifact_sha256,cap,reported_hit_count,search_complete,truncated}, artifacts.structure{artifact_sha256,direct_intervals,inverted_intervals}; provenance.tools[], provenance.databases[]; bundle_sha256. endpoints.scoring_rule: defect_detection_fraction, pristine_bundles_accepted, collapsed_unresolved_state_detected, removed_identity_detected, pair and state validators primary vs independent; base case is the cluster unit; descriptive, cannot support the original integration-advantage claim.

endpoints.question: Technical, model-derived domain recovery: does each tool assign the registered model on shuffled (negative) and 69% fragment (positive) constructs derived from each bundled model's HMMER consensus?
endpoints.inputs: 30 bundled HMM models (te_domains.hmm), one hmmemit -c consensus each; carrier = max(2, ceil(80/L)) consensus copies; per model a full control (admission only), a composition-matched shuffle (negative) and a centered floor(0.69 L) fragment (positive); root seed 410108; SHA-256 counter stream Fisher-Yates. Conditions teagle, hmmer, interproscan, rpsblast_cdd.
endpoints.n_units: 30 models x 3 roles = 90 cases per condition; 60 scored (30 shuffled + 30 fragment), 30 full controls; TEagle TP 30, TN 30, FP 0, FN 0, 30/30 full controls pass; target_hmmer_assigned_call_disagreement_count 0; rpsblast_cdd unsupported on all 90 (PSSMs absent from frozen CDD archive); normalized_row_count 360.
teagle_fields_read: Protocol contract, adapter not inspected: per case, which bundled model was assigned and its significance; per parameter_locks.json domain_thresholds the TEagle domain engine is pyhmmer on the 30-model te_domains.hmm with acceptance field independent_domain_evalue < 0.001 (TEagle record.domains[].evalue = domain i-Evalue), reporting filter full_sequence_evalue <= 0.001, ORF >= 40 aa, longest 12 ORFs, overlapping same-code same-strand hits deduplicated by highest bit score, opposite strands kept. Model identity = record.domains[].hmm (the model NAME); record.domains[].domain is a coarser TEagle code (RT, INT, TPase...).
endpoints.label_space: expected assigned-model detection (full, fragment) or no assigned-model detection (shuffled); scoring_state scored or unsupported.
endpoints.scoring_rule: sensitivity = fragment detected / 30; false_positive_rate = shuffled detected / 30; full controls excluded from metrics; descriptive technical only.

teagle_fields_read: Protocol contract (templates/p2_case_states.tsv and p2_product_calls.tsv), adapter not inspected: per-case operation_state, search_complete, truncated, tool_version, raw_output hash; per product call start_0_based, end_0_based_exclusive, strand, raw_call_label. STATUS: RECORD_FREEZE.json = UNFROZEN; the framework has NEVER executed a scientific stage; no derived_results/raw_results from a real run. require_frozen() refuses to run unless (i) RECORD_FREEZE status FROZEN with valid freeze_id, (ii) the frozen git commit is an ancestor of HEAD, (iii) git diff <v3.8.1 release commit> -- app is EMPTY (so ANY 4.0.0 or 4.1.0 app tree is refused), (iv) Python version/executable/OS/dependency versions (primer3-py, pyhmmer, PySide6, openpyxl, certifi, pypdf) and bundled HMM hash match, (v) every defining file/glob hash matches. benchmark_sets.description: Four evidence levels never pooled: A implementation, B controlled synthetic, C retrospective biological, D prospective external biological. Freeze = clean-checkout create_freeze() hashing 26 defining files plus globs (benchpub/*.py, comparators/*.py, cache/sequences/*.fasta, scripts/*.py, runners/*.py, tests/test_phase*.py), corpus manifest hashes, comparator registry, seeds (synthetic_structure 3812001, robustness 3812002, off_target 3812003, bootstrap 3812004), then a preregistration Zenodo archive before any run; results record only after Windows 10 and Windows 11 clean-machine evidence and a PASS audit. Corpus state: holdout.tsv 109 gradable Level D rows (all curation_status approved, development_exposure none, record_scope element; class CLASS_I 75/CLASS_II 34; order LTR 66, HELITRON 20, TIR 14, LINE 9; superfamily COPIA 16, GYPSY 31, RETROVIRUS 19, TC1_MARINER 12, blank 31; taxon_group plant 47, animal 41, other 14, fungal 7; element_condition fragment 70, other 32, intact 5, internally_deleted 2; 51 organisms; 109 unique sequence hashes; E01 removed 3 duplicates of one 4-accession group; 75 exclusions logged in exclusions.tsv; discovery 184 candidates); negative_controls.tsv 102 rows (100 Level D from 85 accessions + 2 Level B generated); structural_boundaries 1 curated case (STR001, 2 LTR rows); domain_truth 24 rows (12 models x 1 PDB positive + 1 PDB negative); erv_gypsy_challenge 2 rows (ERV001 RETROVIRUS, GYPSY001); de_novo_primer_loci 3; retrospective_assays, wetlab_validation and clean_machine_evidence empty. Holdout breadth gates: >= 3 taxon groups, >= 10 organisms, plant/fungal/animal, orders LTR/LINE/TIR, superfamilies COPIA/GYPSY/RETROVIRUS, element conditions intact/fragment/internally_deleted. TEagle is called IN-PROCESS through engine.analyze (not the GUI) with network disabled.

endpoints.inputs: corpora/holdout.tsv gradable rows; sequence from cache/sequences/<case>.fasta, hash re-verified (sequence_sha256 = hash of residues, headers and whitespace removed, uppercase).

teagle_fields_read: engine.analyze(text, source={'accession','sha256'}) -> result.records[0].classification (stages._single_record: records list must have exactly 1 record)
classification['class'] (substring 'class ii' -> CLASS_II, 'class i' -> CLASS_I, else None)
classification['te_class'] head token before '/' (LTR/LINE/SINE -> same; DNA/TIR/MITE -> TIR; DIRS -> DIRS; otherwise None)
classification['superfamily'] exact string looked up in label_space.teagle_superfamily_map (unmapped string -> None = withheld, silently)

known_limitations: Microsatellite arrays with about 15–20% substitutions can still yield a short (10–19 bp) terminal inverted repeat reported as class unassigned.

A terminal inverted repeat whose own outer end is a run that pairs with itself, such as (TA)n or (GATC)n, cannot be told apart from an insertion into such a run, and the run is cut from the reported arms.

When a transposon whose terminal repeat begins with a run of another unit, such as A(n) or (CA)n, sits in a (TA)n run, the longer of the two runs decides the reported arms: a longer (TA)n run is cut together with the element's own run, and a longer element run leaves the (TA)n run in the arms or loses the terminal repeat. A (TA)n stretch shorter than about 10 bp beside a Tc1/Mariner element is not cut and can lengthen the arms by a few base pairs.
An element flanked by an inverted pair of runs of a unit that cannot pair with itself, such as (CA)n on one side and (TG)n on the other, has its terminal-repeat arms extended into those runs.
A tandem run of 1 kb or more beside an element removes its terminal-repeat candidate, and terminal inverted repeats are searched within about 1.2 kb of each record end.
The microsatellite guard rejects random arms in AT-rich sequence slightly more often than before (at 20% GC, 3.3% of 10-bp and 1.0% of 20-bp arms, against 2.9% and 0.8%).
Analysis-result JSON export of flanked Tc1/Mariner records was fixed during this inventory (CLS-031); any 4.1.0 build made before that fix cannot export those records.
